title.zh: 卷五十六 列傳第四十四: 魏收 魏長賢 魏季景 魏蘭根
title.en: Volume 56 Biographies 44: Wei Shou, Wei Zhangxian, Wei Jijing, Wei Langen
title.raw: 卷五十六 列傳第四十四: 魏收 魏長賢 魏季景 魏蘭根 Volume 56 Biographies 44: Wei Shou, Wei Zhangxian, Wei Jijing, Wei Langen

sentences.zh: 魏收 魏長賢 魏季景 魏蘭根

translations.literal: Wei Shou, Wei Changxian, Wei Jijing, Wei Langen
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, Wei Changxian, Wei Jijing, and Wei Langen

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十四

translations.literal: Biography 44
translations.idiomatic: Biography 44

sentences.zh: 魏收魏長賢魏季景子澹魏蘭根族子愷

translations.literal: Wei Shou; Wei Changxian; Wei Jijing—son Dan; Wei Langen—clansman Kai
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou; Wei Changxian; Wei Jijing (and his son Dan); Wei Langen (and his clansman Kai)

sentences.zh: 魏收，字伯起，小字佛助，钜鹿下曲陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, courtesy name Boqi, childhood name Fozhu, was a native of Xiaquyang in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, whose courtesy name was Boqi and childhood name Fozhu, came from Xiaquyang in Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 自序：漢初魏無知封高良侯，子均。

translations.literal: In his own account of his lineage: In early Han, Wei Wuzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoliang; his son was Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In his own account of the family line: in early Han, Wei Wuzhi was made Marquis of Gaoliang, and his son was Jun.

sentences.zh: 均子恢。

translations.literal: Jun's son was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was succeeded by his son Hui.

sentences.zh: 恢子彥。

translations.literal: Hui's son was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was succeeded by his son Yan.

sentences.zh: 彥子歆，字子胡，幼孤，有志操，博洽經史，位終本郡太守。

translations.literal: Yan's son Xin, courtesy name Zihu, was orphaned in youth but possessed resolve and integrity; he was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories, and died in office as grand administrator of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Xin, courtesy name Zihu, lost his father early yet showed firm purpose; widely read in the classics and histories, he ended his career as grand administrator of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 子悅，字處德，性沉厚，有度量，宣城公趙國李孝伯見而重之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: His son Yue, courtesy name Chude, was of a grave and steady nature and possessed magnanimity; the Marquis of Xuan-cheng, Li Xiaobo of Zhao, saw him and valued him, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, courtesy name Chude, was sober and steady, with breadth of mind; Li Xiaobo of Zhao, Marquis of Xuan-cheng, took a liking to him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 位濟陰太守，以善政稱。

translations.literal: He served as grand administrator of Jiyin and was famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of grand administrator of Jiyin and was known for effective, humane rule.

sentences.zh: 悅子子建，字敬忠，釋褐奉朝請，累遷太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Yue's son Zijian, courtesy name Jingzhong, entered service as a court attendant upon first appointment and was promoted repeatedly to attendant gentleman of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Zijian, courtesy name Jingzhong, began his career as a court attendant and rose step by step to attendant gentleman on the staff of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，宣武時平氏，遂于武興立鎮，尋改為東益州。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the reign of Emperor Xuanwu, when the Di were pacified, a garrison was established at Wuxing and soon renamed Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xuanwu's time, after the Di clans were subdued, a garrison was set up at Wuxing and shortly afterward redesignated Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其後鎮將刺史，乖失人和，群氏作梗，遂為邊患。

translations.literal: Thereafter the garrison commanders and regional inspectors lost the people's goodwill; the tribal clans stirred up trouble and the region became a frontier scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Later garrison commanders and inspectors alienated the populace, the tribal groups turned restive, and the border became chronically troubled.

sentences.zh: 乃除子建東益州刺史。

translations.literal: Zijian was then appointed regional inspector of Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian was then named regional inspector of Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 子建布以恩信，遠近清靜。

translations.literal: Zijian spread favor and trust, and far and near grew tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He governed through kindness and good faith, and peace returned throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，南北二秦城人莫折念生、韓祖香、張長命相繼構逆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, the garrison townsmen of Northern and Southern Er-Qin—Moqi Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming—rose in rebellion one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang 5, the townsmen of the two Qin prefectures north and south—Moqi Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming—staged successive revolts.

sentences.zh: 僉以州城之人，莫不勁勇，同類悉反，宜先收其器械。

translations.literal: All agreed that the people in the prefectural city were every one stalwart and brave, that their kindred had all rebelled, and that their weapons ought first to be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that everyone in the prefectural city was fierce in battle, that their kinsmen had all joined the rebels, and that their arms should be confiscated at once.

sentences.zh: 子建以為城人數當行陣，盡皆驍果，安之足以為用，急之腹背為憂。

translations.literal: Zijian held that the townsmen were men fit for the ranks, all bold and resolute; if reassured they would serve well, but if pressed they would become a danger front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian argued that these townsmen were born soldiers, every one bold; treat them well and they would fight for you, but drive them hard and you would have enemies before and behind.

sentences.zh: 乃悉召居城老壯，曉示之，並上言諸城人本非罪坐而來者，悉求聽免。

translations.literal: He therefore summoned all the old and young living in the city, explained the situation to them, and memorialized that the various townsmen had not come as convicted criminals and should all be allowed to go home.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered every adult and elder in the city, explained his policy to them, and petitioned that these settlers—most of whom had not been sent as convicts—be permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 明帝優詔從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued a gracious edict granting his request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming approved the request with a favorable edict.

sentences.zh: 子建漸分其父兄子弟，外居郡戍，內外相顧，終獲保全。

translations.literal: Zijian gradually dispersed fathers, elder brothers, and younger kinsmen to live at outlying commandery posts, so that inside and outside could watch over one another, and in the end all were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually sent fathers, brothers, and younger kin to garrison towns in the commanderies so that families could support one another from within and without, and in the end everyone was kept safe.

sentences.zh: 及秦賊乘勝，屯營黑水，子建乃潛使掩襲，前後斬獲甚眾，威名赫然。

translations.literal: When the Qin rebels pressed their advantage and encamped at Heishui, Zijian secretly sent men to strike by surprise; before and after, they slew and captured a great host, and his renown blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: As the Qin rebels followed up their victories and camped on the Heishui, he launched a secret raid; the slaughter and captures were immense, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 先反者，及此悉降。

translations.literal: Those who had rebelled earlier now all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier rebels all surrendered at this point.

sentences.zh: 乃間使上聞，帝甚嘉之，詔子建兼尚書，為行台刺史如故。

translations.literal: He then sent word through an intermediary; the emperor greatly praised him and ordered Zijian to serve concurrently as Minister of the Secretariat, while remaining regional inspector on the mobile headquarters staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: He reported through a secret channel; the emperor was much pleased and named Zijian concurrent Minister of the Secretariat, while he continued as regional inspector on the frontier headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 於是威振蜀土。

translations.literal: His authority now shook the lands of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His prestige now dominated the Shu region.

sentences.zh: 其梁、巴、二益、兩秦之事，皆所節度。

translations.literal: Affairs of Liang, Ba, the two Yizhou regions, and the two Qin prefectures all fell under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He held overall authority over Liang, Ba, the two Yizhou districts, and the two Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史傅豎眼子敬仲心以為愧，在洛大行貨賄，以圖行台。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan, regional inspector of Liangzhou, felt ashamed at heart because his son Jingzhong had been outshone; in Luoyang he lavished bribes on a grand scale to win the frontier headquarters post.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan of Liangzhou, stung because his son Jingzhong had been eclipsed, spent heavily on bribes in Luoyang to secure the frontier headquarters command.

sentences.zh: 先是子建亦屢求歸京師，至此，乃遣刺史唐永代焉。

translations.literal: Zijian had long before repeatedly asked to return to the capital; at this point he was replaced by the regional inspector Tang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian had for some time been petitioning to return to the capital; now Tang Yong was sent to replace him as regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 豎眼因為行台。

translations.literal: Shuyan was accordingly made head of the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan was appointed to head the frontier headquarters in his place.

sentences.zh: 子建將還，群氏慕戀，相率斷道。

translations.literal: As Zijian was about to return, the tribal clans, cherishing him, banded together and blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijian prepared to leave, the tribal peoples, unwilling to part with him, massed together and cut the road.

sentences.zh: 主簿楊僧覆先行曉喻，諸氏忿曰：「我留刺史，爾送出也？」

translations.literal: The registrar Yang Sengfu went ahead to explain, but the tribesmen said in anger, "We are keeping our inspector—are you escorting him out?"
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Yang Sengfu rode ahead to reason with them, but the tribesmen cried in anger, "We mean to keep our inspector—are you the ones sending him away?"

sentences.zh: 斫之數創，幾死。

translations.literal: They hacked him with many wounds, and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: They hacked him repeatedly and left him near death.

sentences.zh: 子建徐加慰譬，旬月方得前行。

translations.literal: Zijian slowly added words of comfort and persuasion, and only after a month or more could the party move on.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian soothed them with patient persuasion, and only after a full month could the party resume its journey.

sentences.zh: 吏人贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Gifts from officials and commoners he accepted not a single one.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift offered by officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 而東益氏、蜀尋反，攻逼唐永，永棄城而走，乃喪一籓矣。

translations.literal: Soon the tribes of Eastern Yizhou and Shu rebelled again, pressed Tang Yong, and Yong abandoned the city and fled—the frontier prefecture was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Eastern Yizhou tribes and the Shu peoples rose again, besieged Tang Yong, and Yong fled the city—the region was lost to the realm.

sentences.zh: 初永之走，子建客有沙門雲璨及钜鹿人耿顯皆沒落氏手，及知子建之客，垂泣追衣物還之，送出白馬。

translations.literal: When Yong fled, two of Zijian's retainers—the monk Yuncan and Geng Xian of Julu—fell into tribal hands; learning they were Zijian's guests, the tribesmen wept, pursued them to return their belongings, and escorted them out at Baima.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fled, two of Zijian's companions—the monk Yuncan and Geng Xian of Julu—were seized by the tribes; once they learned these men were Zijian's guests, they wept, restored their goods, and saw them safely out at Baima.

sentences.zh: 遺愛所被如此。

translations.literal: Such was the reach of the affection he left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of affection he had won.

sentences.zh: 初，子建為前軍將軍，十年不徙，在洛閒暇，與吏部尚書李歆、歆從弟延寔頗為弈棋，時人謂為耽好。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Zijian served as General of the Vanguard for ten years without transfer, idle in Luoyang he often played chess with Li Xin, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Xin's younger cousin Yanbao; people of the time called this an absorbing pastime.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during ten years as General of the Vanguard without a new posting, he had leisure in Luoyang and often played chess with Li Xin, Minister of Personnel, and Xin's cousin Yanbao—contemporaries said he was addicted to the game.

sentences.zh: 子建每曰：「棋于廉勇之際，得之深矣。

translations.literal: Zijian would say, "In chess one grasps the turning point between integrity and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian used to say, "Chess teaches you the balance between caution and boldness.

sentences.zh: 且吾未為時用，博弈可也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, I am not yet employed by the age—gaming is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the times have no use for me yet—a game is harmless enough."

sentences.zh: 及一臨邊事，凡經五年，未曾對局。

translations.literal: Once he took up frontier affairs, for five full years he never played a match.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took charge on the border, he played no game at all for five years.

sentences.zh: 還洛後，累遷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: After returning to Luoyang he was promoted repeatedly to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After his return to Luoyang he rose step by step to Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 初，元顥內逼，莊帝北幸，子建謂所親盧義僖曰：「北海自絕社稷，稱籓蕭衍，吾老矣，豈能為陪臣！」

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward and Emperor Zhuang fled north, Zijian said to his intimate Lu Yixi, "The Prince of Beihai has cut himself off from the altars of state and declared himself a vassal of Xiao Yan—I am old; how could I become a subject in attendance!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao threatened the capital and Emperor Zhuang fled north, Zijian told his friend Lu Yixi, "The Prince of Beihai has renounced the dynasty and bowed to Xiao Yan of Liang—I am too old to play the courtier to a usurper!"

sentences.zh: 遂攜家口居洛南。

translations.literal: He thereupon moved his household to live south of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: With that he moved his family to the south bank of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 顥平乃歸。

translations.literal: When Hao was pacified he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He came back only after Yuan Hao was defeated.

sentences.zh: 先苦風痹，及此遂甚。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from wind paralysis, and now it grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been afflicted with rheumatic paralysis, and now the condition worsened sharply.

sentences.zh: 以卿任有務，屢上書乞身，特除右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because his post as Commandant entailed duties, he repeatedly memorialized to resign; he was specially appointed Grand Master of Splendid Brightness on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the duties of his office too heavy, he petitioned repeatedly to retire and was specially named Grand Master of Splendid Brightness of the Right.

sentences.zh: 邢杲之平，太傅李延寔子侍中彧為大使，撫慰東土。

translations.literal: After Xing Gao was pacified, Li Yanbao's son Yu, Palace Attendant, was made chief envoy to console the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Gao's rebellion was put down, Yu—son of the Grand Tutor Li Yanbao and a palace attendant—was sent as chief envoy to reassure the east.

sentences.zh: 時外戚貴盛，送客填門，子建亦往候別。

translations.literal: At the time the consort kin were exalted and powerful; farewell visitors filled the gate, and Zijian also went to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial in-laws were then at the height of power, and well-wishers thronged the gate; Zijian went too, to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 延實曰：「小兒今行，何以相助？」

translations.literal: Yanbao said, "My boy is setting out today—how will you help him?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbao asked, "My son leaves today—what counsel can you give him?"

sentences.zh: 子建曰：「益以盈滿為誡。」

translations.literal: Zijian said, "Let him take fullness and excess as his warning."
translations.idiomatic: Zijian replied, "Tell him to beware of reaching the peak."

sentences.zh: 延實悵然久之。

translations.literal: Yanbao was long lost in somber thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbao fell silent for a long while, deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝殺爾硃榮，遇禍于河陰者，其家率相吊賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang killed Erzhu Rong, the families of those who met disaster at Heyin for the most part offered condolences and congratulations to one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang killed Erzhu Rong, the kin of those slaughtered at Heyin mostly exchanged condolences—and congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太尉李虔第二子仁曜，子建之女婿，往亦見害。

translations.literal: Li Qian the Grand Commandant's second son Renyao, Zijian's son-in-law, was also killed on that occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Renyao, second son of Grand Commandant Li Qian and Zijian's son-in-law, was among those killed.

sentences.zh: 子建謂姨弟盧道虔曰：「朝廷誅翦權強，凶徒尚梗，未聞有奇謀異略，恐不可濟。

translations.literal: Zijian said to his cousin on his mother's side, Lu Daoqian, "The court has cut down the mighty, yet the violent still obstruct the way; I have heard no extraordinary stratagem or plan—I fear success is unlikely.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian told his cousin Lu Daoqian, "The court has struck down the powerful, but the ringleaders are still loose, and I hear of no bold plan to finish the work—I doubt this will end well.

sentences.zh: 此乃李門禍始，吊賀無乃匆匆！」

translations.literal: This is but the beginning of calamity for the Li clan—are condolences and congratulations not rather hasty!"
translations.idiomatic: This is only the start of trouble for the Li family—aren't your condolences and congratulations a bit premature!"

sentences.zh: 及永安之後，李氏宗族流離，或遇誅夷，如其所慮。

translations.literal: After the Yong'an era the Li clan was scattered and uprooted; some met execution and extermination, just as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yong'an period the Li kindred were driven into exile or put to death, exactly as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 後曆左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Master of Splendid Brightness on the left and was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the post of Left Grand Master of Splendid Brightness and was further named Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子建自出為籓牧，董司山南，居脂膏之中，遇天下多事，正身潔已，不以財利經懷。

translations.literal: From the time Zijian went out as a frontier governor and oversaw the lands south of the mountains, dwelling amid the richest territories while the realm was in turmoil, he kept himself upright and pure and let wealth and profit never cross his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Once he left the capital to govern the south, he ruled a rich province in an age of chaos yet kept his conduct clean and never let gain guide his decisions.

sentences.zh: 及歸京師，家人衣食，常不周贍，清素之跡，著於終始。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, his household's food and clothing were often insufficient; the record of his frugality and integrity runs from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital his family often lacked enough to live on, yet his reputation for austerity never wavered from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 性存重慎，不雜交遊，唯與尚書盧義僖、姨弟涇州刺史盧道裕雅相親昵。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave and cautious and did not mix in wide social circles; only with the Minister of the Secretariat Lu Yixi and his cousin Lu Daoyu, regional inspector of Jingzhou, was he on terms of warm intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature cautious and reserved in company, confiding only in Minister Lu Yixi and his cousin Lu Daoyu, regional inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，顧敕二子曰：「死生大分，含氣所同。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave he turned and charged his two sons, saying, "Life and death are the great division—all who draw breath share it alike.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he called his two sons and said, "Life and death are the great divide—every living soul must face it.

sentences.zh: 世有厚葬，吾平生不取；

translations.literal: The world favors lavish burial, which I have never accepted in my life;
translations.idiomatic: The world loves lavish funerals, but I have never approved of them;

sentences.zh: 遽除裸身，又非吾意。

translations.literal: to strip the body bare at once is likewise not my wish.
translations.idiomatic: nor do I wish to be laid out naked, as some now do.

sentences.zh: 氣絕之後，斂以時服。

translations.literal: After my breath is gone, dress me in the garments of the season.
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, dress me in ordinary clothes of the day.

sentences.zh: 吾平生契闊，前後三娶，合葬之事，抑又非古。

translations.literal: In my life I have been bound and parted by marriage, taking three wives in succession; joint burial, moreover, is not the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: I have married three times in the course of my life; joint burial, besides, is not the old custom.

sentences.zh: 且汝二母，先在舊塋，墳地久固，已有定別。

translations.literal: Your two mothers already rest in the old cemetery; the ground has long been fixed, and their places are settled.
translations.idiomatic: Your first two mothers lie already in the family graveyard—their plots are long established and should not be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 唯汝次母墓在外耳，可遷入兆域，依班而定行於吾墓之後，如此足矣，不須附合。

translations.literal: Only your second mother's tomb lies outside; she may be moved into the burial precinct and, according to rank, placed in the row behind my tomb—that is enough; there is no need to join graves.
translations.idiomatic: Only your stepmother's grave lies elsewhere; move her into the family ground and, by proper order, set her row behind mine—that will suffice; do not bury us together in one mound.

sentences.zh: 當順吾心，勿令吾有遺恨。」

translations.literal: You must follow my heart and not let me die with regret."
translations.idiomatic: Do as I ask, so that I may die without regret."

sentences.zh: 永熙二年春，卒於洛陽孝義裏舍，時年六十。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Yongxi he died at his residence in Xiaoyi Lane in Luoyang, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in spring of Yongxi 2 at his home in Xiaoyi Lane, Luoyang, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 又贈儀同三司、定州刺史，諡曰文靜。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Three Excellencies of Equal Honor and made regional inspector of Dingzhou; his posthumous title was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored with the Three Excellencies of Equal Rank and the title regional inspector of Dingzhou; his temple name was Wenjing, "Cultured and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 二子，收、祚。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Shou and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Shou and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 收少機警，不持細行。

translations.literal: Shou in youth was quick-witted but careless in small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shou was clever but careless about propriety in small matters.

sentences.zh: 年十五，頗已屬文。

translations.literal: At fifteen he could already compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he was already writing creditable prose.

sentences.zh: 及隨父赴邊，好習騎射，欲以武藝自達。

translations.literal: When he followed his father to the frontier he delighted in practicing horsemanship and archery, hoping to make his way by martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: When he went with his father to the border he took up riding and archery, hoping to rise by military prowess.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭伯調之曰：「魏郎弄戟多少？」

translations.literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him, saying, "Young Wei, how well do you handle the halberd?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo of Xingyang mocked him: "Master Wei, how many tricks do you know with a halberd?"

sentences.zh: 收慚，遂折節讀書。

translations.literal: Shou was ashamed and thereupon restrained himself and took up study.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, he turned from arms to books.

sentences.zh: 夏月，坐板床，隨樹陰諷誦。

translations.literal: In summer he would sit on a plank bed and, following the shade of the trees, chant his texts aloud.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he sat on a plain plank bed, moving with the shade of the trees as he recited his texts.

sentences.zh: 積年，床板為之銳減，而精力不輟。

translations.literal: Year after year the bed planks were worn thin by it, yet his energy never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years the boards were worn paper-thin, yet he never slackened his effort.

sentences.zh: 以文華顯。

translations.literal: He became renowned for literary brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: He won fame through literary talent.

sentences.zh: 初除太學博士。

translations.literal: His first appointment was as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His first post was Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮于河陰濫害朝士，收亦在圍中，以日晏獲免。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong wantonly slaughtered court officials at Heyin, Shou was also among those surrounded, but because night was falling he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong massacred court officials at Heyin, Shou was caught in the roundup but was spared because dusk was falling.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神雋重收才學，奏授司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, valued Shou's talent and learning and memorialized to appoint him recorder on the staff of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Minister of Personnel, admired his gifts and had him named recorder on the Minister of State's staff.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，除北主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was appointed Director of the Northern Hosts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 3 he was made Director of the Northern Hosts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝立，妙簡近侍，詔試收為封禪書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin ascended the throne, close attendants were carefully chosen; Shou was ordered tested by composing a fengshan memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin came to the throne and chose his inner circle with care, Shou was commanded to draft a fengshan proclamation as a trial.

sentences.zh: 收下筆便就，不立槁草，文將千言，所改無幾。

translations.literal: Shou set brush to paper and finished at once, making no draft; the text ran to nearly a thousand words, with scarcely any revisions.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote it straight off without a draft—nearly a thousand words, with hardly a change.

sentences.zh: 時黃門郎賈思同侍立，深奇之，白帝曰：「雖七步之才，無以過此。」

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Jia Sitong stood in attendance and was deeply amazed; he reported to the emperor, "Even the talent of seven paces could not surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sitong, Yellow Gate Gentleman, stood by in wonder and told the emperor, "Not even Cao Zhi's gift at seven paces could match this."

sentences.zh: 遷散騎侍郎，尋敕典起居注，並修國史，俄兼中書侍郎，時年二十六。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, soon ordered to take charge of the imperial diary and to compile the national history, and shortly thereafter made concurrent Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat—he was twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, soon put in charge of the imperial diary and the national history, and not long after named concurrent Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat—at twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，又詔收攝本職，文誥填積，事咸稱旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was again ordered to resume his former duties; edicts and proclamations piled up, and in every matter he met the emperor's pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was recalled to his posts; imperial documents piled up, and everything he wrote pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎崔甗從齊神武入朝，熏灼於世，收初不詣門。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Yan, who had entered court with Qi Shenwu, blazed with influence in the world; at first Shou did not call at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan of the Yellow Gate, who had come to court with Gao Huan of Northern Qi, was the man of the hour; Shou at first refused to pay court to him.

sentences.zh: 甗為帝登阼赦云：「朕托體孝文。」

translations.literal: Yan drafted the amnesty for the emperor's accession, saying, "We take our bodily form from Emperor Xiaowen."
translations.idiomatic: Yan wrote the accession amnesty with the line, "Our person derives from Emperor Xiaowen."

sentences.zh: 收嗤其率直。

translations.literal: Shou mocked its bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Shou laughed at its bluntness.

sentences.zh: 正員郎李慎以告之，甗深忿忌。

translations.literal: The regular gentleman Li Shen told Yan of this, and Yan bore deep resentment and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, a regular gentleman, repeated the remark to Yan, who nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 時節閔帝殂，令收為詔。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Jiemin died, and Shou was ordered to draft the edict of announcement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin died, Shou was ordered to draft the mourning edict.

sentences.zh: 甗乃宣言：收普泰世出入幃幄，一日造詔，優為詞旨，然則義旗之士，盡為逆人。

translations.literal: Yan then proclaimed publicly: "In the Putai era Shou went in and out of the inner chambers; in a single day he drafts an edict with polished wording—then all who raised the banner of righteousness become rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Yan then declared openly: "In the Putai era Shou haunted the inner chambers; he can turn out a polished edict in a day—by which token every man who took up arms for the righteous cause becomes a traitor."

sentences.zh: 又收父老，合解官歸侍。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shou's father was old and ought to resign office and return home to be served.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Shou's father was elderly and that Shou ought to resign and go home to care for him.

sentences.zh: 南台將加彈劾，賴尚書辛雄為言于中尉綦俊，乃解。

translations.literal: The Southern Terrace was about to impeach him, but thanks to the Minister of the Secretariat Xin Xiong speaking on his behalf to the Commandant of Justice Qi Jun, the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate was ready to impeach him, but Minister Xin Xiong pleaded with Commandant of Justice Qi Jun, and the charge was dropped.

sentences.zh: 收有賤生弟仲同，先未齒錄，因此怖懼，上籍，遣還鄉扶侍。

translations.literal: Shou had a younger brother by a concubine, Zhongtong, who had not been entered in the family register; in fear because of this, he registered him and sent him back to the village to support and serve their father.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had a half-brother Zhongtong, born to a concubine and never entered in the register; frightened by the scandal, he entered him on the rolls and sent him home to care for their father.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗大發士卒，狩于嵩山之南，旬有六日。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once mobilized troops on a great scale and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu once mustered a huge force and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days.

sentences.zh: 時寒，朝野嗟怨。

translations.literal: The weather was cold, and court and commoners alike lamented in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The season was bitterly cold, and the whole realm groaned in protest.

sentences.zh: 帝與從官及諸妃王，奇伎異飾，多非禮度。

translations.literal: The emperor, together with attendants and the various consorts and princes, [presented] exotic performances and unusual adornments, mostly contrary to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, his attendants, and the consorts and princes indulged in exotic entertainments and outlandish finery, most of it in breach of proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 收欲言則懼，欲默不能已，乃上《南狩賦》以諷焉，年二十七。

translations.literal: Shou wished to speak but feared; wished to keep silent but could not restrain himself; he therefore submitted the "Southern Hunt Rhapsody" to admonish indirectly—he was twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Shou wanted to speak out but was afraid; wanted to hold his tongue but could not. He submitted his "Southern Hunt Rhapsody" as an indirect remonstrance. He was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 雖富言淫麗，而終歸雅正。

translations.literal: Although rich in language and florid, it ultimately returned to elegant correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Though lavish and ornate in expression, the piece ultimately returned to refined propriety.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔報焉，甚見褒美。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a personal handwritten edict, greatly praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a personal edict in his own hand, lavishing praise upon him.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯謂曰：「卿不遇老夫，猶應逐兔。」

translations.literal: Zheng Bo said to him: "Had you not met this old man, you would still be chasing rabbits."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo said to him, "If you had not met me, you would still be out chasing rabbits."

sentences.zh: 神武固讓天柱大將軍，魏帝敕收為詔，令遂所請。

translations.literal: Gao Huan firmly declined the title Tianzhu Grand General; the Wei emperor ordered Shou to draft the edict, commanding that his request be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan firmly declined the post of Tianzhu Grand General. The Wei emperor ordered Shou to draft an edict granting the request.

sentences.zh: 欲加相國，問收相國品秩，收以實對，帝遂止。

translations.literal: They wished to add the title Chancellor; they asked Shou about the Chancellor's rank and grade; Shou answered truthfully; the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When they wished to confer the title of Chancellor, they asked Shou about its rank and grade. Shou answered truthfully, and the emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 收既未測主、相之意，以前事不安，求解，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Shou, having not yet fathomed the intentions of the ruler and the chancellor, was uneasy about past matters and requested dismissal; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to read the minds of the emperor and the chancellor, and still unsettled by past events, Shou asked to resign. An edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 久之，除帝兄子廣平王贊開府從事中郎，收不敢辭，乃為《庭竹賦》以致已意。

translations.literal: After some time, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the establishment of the Prince of Guangping, Zan, the emperor's nephew; Shou did not dare refuse, and therefore composed the "Courtyard Bamboo Rhapsody" to convey his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the household of the emperor's nephew, Prince Zan of Guangping. Shou did not dare refuse, and wrote the "Courtyard Bamboo Rhapsody" to express what he felt.

sentences.zh: 尋兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served concurrently as a Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 與濟陰溫子升、河間邢子才齊譽，世號「三才」。

translations.literal: Together with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian he shared equal renown; the age called them the "Three Talents."
translations.idiomatic: He was ranked alongside Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian, and the age called them the "Three Talents."

sentences.zh: 時孝武內有間隙，收遂以疾固辭而免。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu had internal rifts; Shou therefore firmly declined on grounds of illness and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was then riven by internal discord, and Shou firmly pleaded illness until he was released from office.

sentences.zh: 舅崔孝芬怪而問之，收曰：「懼有晉陽之甲。」

translations.literal: His uncle Cui Xiaofen found it strange and asked him; Shou said: "I fear there will be armed forces from Jinyang."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cui Xiaofen thought it odd and asked why. Shou said, "I fear there will be armed men from Jinyang."

sentences.zh: 尋而神武南上，帝西入關。

translations.literal: Soon after, Gao Huan marched south, and the emperor entered the Pass to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Gao Huan marched south while the emperor fled west through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 收兼通直散騎常侍，副王昕聘梁。

translations.literal: Shou also served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Palace Library and as deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shou also served as Regular Attendant of the Palace Library and went to Liang as Wang Xin's deputy on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 昕風流文辯，收辭藻富逸，梁主及其群臣咸加敬異。

translations.literal: Xin was elegant and eloquent in letters; Shou's diction was rich and flowing; the Liang ruler and his entire court all showed them special respect and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was graceful and quick with words; Shou's prose was lush and fluent. The Liang ruler and his entire court treated them with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 先是，南北初和，李諧、盧元明首通使命，二人才器，並為鄰國所重。

translations.literal: Previously, when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming were the first to carry envoys; both men's talent and capacity were equally valued by the neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming had been the first envoys exchanged, and both were highly regarded in the neighboring court.

sentences.zh: 至此，梁主稱曰：「盧、李命世，王、魏中興，未知後來，復何如耳。」

translations.literal: At this point the Liang ruler said: "Lu and Li were talents of their age; Wang and Wei renew the cause—who knows how those to come will compare?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Liang ruler said, "Lu and Li were talents of their generation; Wang and Wei revive the tradition. Who knows what those who come after will be like?"

sentences.zh: 收在館，遂買吳婢入館；

translations.literal: While lodged in the guest house, Shou then bought a Wu slave girl and brought her into the quarters;
translations.idiomatic: While staying in the embassy lodge, Shou bought a Wu slave girl and brought her inside;

sentences.zh: 其部下有賣婢者，收亦喚取，遍行奸穢。

translations.literal: when there were slave girls for sale among his attendants, Shou also summoned and took them, committing lewd acts everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: whenever slave girls were offered among his attendants, he summoned them too and debauched them without restraint.

sentences.zh: 梁朝館司，皆為之獲罪。

translations.literal: The Liang guest-house officials all got into trouble because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang officials in charge of the guest house were all punished for it.

sentences.zh: 人稱其才，而鄙其行。

translations.literal: People praised his talent but despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: People praised his talent but scorned his behavior.

sentences.zh: 在途作《聘遊賦》，辭甚美盛。

translations.literal: On the journey he composed the "Rhapsody on the Diplomatic Tour"; the wording was extremely splendid.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he wrote the "Rhapsody on the Diplomatic Tour," a piece of exceptionally fine prose.

sentences.zh: 使還，尚書右僕射高隆之求南貨於昕、收，不能如志，遂諷御史中尉高仲密禁止昕、收於其台，久之得釋。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Longzhi asked Xin and Shou for southern goods; unable to obtain what he wished, he hinted to Commandant of Justice Gao Zhongmi to detain Xin and Shou at his bureau; after a long time they were released.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission returned, Vice Director Gao Longzhi asked Xin and Shou for southern goods. When they could not satisfy him, he prompted Commandant of Justice Gao Zhongmi to detain them at the censorate. Only after a long while were they released.

sentences.zh: 及孫搴死，司馬子如薦收，召赴晉陽，以為中外府主簿。

translations.literal: When Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou; he was summoned to Jinyang and appointed chief secretary of the combined internal and external offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou. He was summoned to Jinyang and made chief secretary of the combined internal and external offices.

sentences.zh: 以受旨乖懺，頻被嫌責，加以箠楚，久不得志。

translations.literal: Because he fell short in receiving orders, he was repeatedly blamed and criticized, also beaten with rods; for a long time he could not achieve his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly failed to carry out orders as expected, was often blamed and rebuked, and was beaten with rods. For a long time he could not make his way.

sentences.zh: 會司馬子如奉使霸朝，收假其餘光。

translations.literal: When Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court, Shou borrowed the reflected glory.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court, Shou basked in his reflected prestige.

sentences.zh: 子如因宴戲言于神武曰：「魏收，天子中書郎，一國大才，願大王借與顏色。」

translations.literal: Ziru, at a banquet in jest, said to Gao Huan: "Wei Shou, the Son of Heaven's Secretariat Gentleman—a great talent of the realm—my lord, please show him some favor."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Ziru said playfully to Gao Huan, "Wei Shou is a Secretariat Gentleman of the Son of Heaven and a great talent of the realm. My lord, please show him a little kindness."

sentences.zh: 由此轉府屬，然未甚優禮。

translations.literal: Because of this he was transferred to staff of the office, but still was not treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was transferred to staff duty in the office, though he still did not receive much special treatment.

sentences.zh: 收從叔季景有文學，曆官著名，並在收前，然收常所欺忽。

translations.literal: Shou's clansman uncle Ji Jing had literary learning, held famous offices in succession, all before Shou; yet Shou often slighted and overlooked him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's clansman uncle Ji Jing was a man of letters who had held distinguished posts in succession, all of them before Shou's own rise, yet Shou often treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 季景、收初赴並，頓丘李庶者，故大司農諧之子也，以華辯見稱，曾謂收曰：「霸朝便有二魏。」

translations.literal: When Ji Jing and Shou first went to Bing, there was Li Shu of Dunqiu, son of the former Minister of Finance Xie, famed for splendid eloquence; he once said to Shou: "The hegemonic court already has two Weis."
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Jing and Shou first went to Bing, there was Li Shu of Dunqiu, son of the former Minister of Finance Li Xie, famed for his brilliant eloquence. He once said to Shou, "The hegemonic court already has two Weis."

sentences.zh: 收率爾曰：「以從叔見比，例邪輸之比卿。」

translations.literal: Shou offhandedly said: "Comparing me to my clansman uncle—by the same rule, Xie Yu is like you."
translations.idiomatic: Shou blurted out, "If I am matched with my clansman uncle, then by the same logic Xie Yu is your match."

sentences.zh: 邪輸者，故尚書令陳留公繼伯之子，愚癡有名，好自入市肆，高價買物，商買共所嗤玩。

translations.literal: Xie Yu was the son of the former Minister of the Secretariat, the Duke of Chenliu, Ji Bo; he was famous for foolishness, liked to go to markets himself and buy things at high prices—merchants all mocked and made sport of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yu was the son of the former Minister Ji Bo, Duke of Chenliu. He was notorious for stupidity, loved to go into the markets himself and pay inflated prices for goods, and the traders all laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 收忽以季景方之，不遜例多如此。

translations.literal: Shou suddenly compared Ji Jing to him—many instances of such disrespect were like this.
translations.idiomatic: That Shou should suddenly compare Ji Jing to Xie Yu was typical of his habitual insolence.

sentences.zh: 收本以文才，必望穎脫見知，位既不遂，求修國史。

translations.literal: Shou originally by literary talent certainly hoped to emerge and be recognized; when rank did not succeed, he sought to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had counted on his literary gifts to win recognition and rise; when advancement failed him, he asked to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 崔暹為言于文襄曰：「國史事重，公家父子霸王功業，皆須具載，非收不可。」

translations.literal: Cui Xuan spoke on his behalf to Gao Cheng, saying: "The national history is weighty; your family's father-and-son hegemonic achievements must all be fully recorded—Shou is indispensable."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan spoke to Gao Cheng on his behalf: "The national history is a weighty matter. Your family's hegemonic achievements, father and son together, must all be fully recorded, and no one but Shou can do it."

sentences.zh: 文襄乃啟收兼散騎常侍，修國史。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng then petitioned that Shou additionally serve as Regular Cavalry Attendant and compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng then petitioned that Shou be appointed Regular Cavalry Attendant and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 武定二年，除正常侍，領兼中書侍郎，仍修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding, he was appointed Regular Attendant, concurrently serving as Secretariat Vice Director, and still compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently Secretariat Vice Director, and continued to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 魏帝宴百僚，問何故名「人日」，皆莫能知。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor feasted the hundred officials and asked why it was called "Human Day"; none could say.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the hundred officials, the Wei emperor asked why the day was called "Human Day." No one could answer.

sentences.zh: 收對曰：「晉議郎董勳答問禮俗云：正月一日為雞，二日為狗，三日為豬，四日為羊，五日為牛，六日為馬，七日為人。」

translations.literal: Shou replied: "The Jin Protocol Gentleman Dong Xun, answering questions on rites and customs, said: the first day of the first month is the chicken, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, and the seventh the human."
translations.idiomatic: Shou answered, "The Jin Protocol Gentleman Dong Xun, in his answers on rites and customs, said that the first day of the first month is the Day of the Chicken, the second the Day of the Dog, the third the Day of the Pig, the fourth the Day of the Sheep, the fifth the Day of the Ox, the sixth the Day of the Horse, and the seventh the Day of the Human."

sentences.zh: 時邢邵亦在側，甚恧焉。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Shao was also at his side and was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao was standing nearby at the time and was deeply embarrassed.

sentences.zh: 自魏、梁和好，書下紙每云：「想彼境內寧靜，此率土安和。」

translations.literal: Since Wei and Liang made peace, documents always said: "May your realm within be tranquil; this land under Heaven be peaceful and harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Liang made peace, their diplomatic letters had routinely read, "May your realm within be tranquil; may this land under Heaven be peaceful and harmonious."

sentences.zh: 梁後使其書乃去「彼」字，自稱猶著「此」，欲示無外之意。

translations.literal: Later Liang had their documents remove the word "your" while still keeping "this" for themselves, wishing to show there was no outside or other.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang had the word for "your" dropped from its letters while still keeping "this" for itself, intending to suggest that there was no outside world.

sentences.zh: 收定報書云：「想境內清晏，今萬國安和。」

translations.literal: Shou fixed the reply document to say: "May the realm within be clear and calm; now the myriad states be peaceful and harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: Shou fixed the reply formula to read, "May the realm within be clear and calm; may the myriad states now be peaceful and harmonious."

sentences.zh: 梁人復書，依以為體。

translations.literal: The people of Liang, in their replies, followed this as the standard form.
translations.idiomatic: In their replies, the Liang side adopted this as the standard form.

sentences.zh: 後神武入朝，靜帝授相國，固讓，令收為啟。

translations.literal: Later Gao Huan came to court; Emperor Jing conferred the Chancellorship; he firmly declined; he ordered Shou to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Huan came to court. Emperor Jing offered him the Chancellorship, and when he firmly declined, Gao Huan had Shou draft the memorial of refusal.

sentences.zh: 啟成呈上，文襄時侍側，神武指收曰「此人當復為崔光。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished and presented, Gao Cheng was attending at his side; Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said, "This man should again become a Cui Guang."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was finished and presented, Gao Cheng was in attendance at his side. Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said, "This man will be another Cui Guang."

sentences.zh: 四年，神武於西門豹祠宴集，謂司馬子如曰：「魏收為史官，書吾善惡，聞北便利時諸貴常餉史官飲食，司馬僕射頗曾餉不？」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at a banquet at the shrine of Ximen Bao, Gao Huan said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou as historiographer writes my good and evil; I hear that in the northern regions the nobles often provided food and drink to historiographers—Vice Director Sima, did you ever provide any?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, at a banquet at the shrine of Ximen Bao, Gao Huan said to Sima Ziru, "Wei Shou is the historiographer who records my good and evil deeds. I hear that in the north the great families often treated historiographers to food and drink. Vice Director Sima, did you ever treat him?"

sentences.zh: 因共大笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon all laughed together.
translations.idiomatic: At that they all burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 仍謂收曰：「卿勿見元康等在吾目下趨走，謂吾以為勤勞。

translations.literal: He still said to Shou: "Do not see Yuankang and the others scurrying before my eyes and think I consider this diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Shou, "Do not see Yuankang and the others scurrying before my eyes and think I mistake that for real diligence.

sentences.zh: 我後世身名在卿手，勿謂我不知。」

translations.literal: My posterity's person and name are in your hands—do not think I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: My reputation in posterity is in your hands. Do not imagine I do not know it."

sentences.zh: 尋加兼著作郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 收昔在京洛，輕薄尤甚，人號云「魏收驚蛺蝶。」

translations.literal: Shou formerly in the capital was extremely frivolous; people called him, saying, "Wei Shou the butterfly-startler."
translations.idiomatic: In the old capital Shou had been notoriously frivolous, and people called him "Wei Shou the Butterfly-Startler."

sentences.zh: 文襄曾遊東山，令給事黃門侍郎顥等宴。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng once toured Eastern Hill and had Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yan and others hold a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng once visited Eastern Hill and had Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yang Yan and others hold a banquet.

sentences.zh: 文襄曰：「魏收恃才無宜適，須出其短。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng said: "Wei Shou relies on his talent and is insufferable—we must expose his flaws."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "Wei Shou is insufferably proud of his talent. We must expose his weak points."

sentences.zh: 往復數番，收忽大唱曰：「楊遵彥理屈，已倒。」

translations.literal: After several exchanges back and forth, Shou suddenly shouted loudly: "Yang Zunyan's argument is defeated—he has fallen."
translations.idiomatic: After several rounds of debate, Shou suddenly cried out, "Yang Zunyan's argument is broken—he has fallen!"

sentences.zh: 愔從容曰：「我綽有餘暇，山立不動。

translations.literal: Yang Yan calmly said: "I am ample with spare leisure—standing like a mountain, unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan replied calmly, "I am ample and unhurried, standing like a mountain and unmoved.

sentences.zh: 若遇當塗，恐翩翩遂逝。」

translations.literal: If one meets 'the one on the road,' I fear he would flutter away."
translations.idiomatic: But if he met 'the one on the road,' I fear he would flutter away at once."

sentences.zh: 當塗者魏，翩翩者蝶也。

translations.literal: 'The one on the road' is Wei; 'fluttering' is the butterfly.
translations.idiomatic: 'The one on the road' meant Wei; 'fluttering' meant butterfly.

sentences.zh: 文襄先知之，大笑稱善。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng had foreseen it beforehand and laughed greatly, praising it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng had seen the barb coming and laughed heartily in approval.

sentences.zh: 文襄又曰：「向語猶微，宜更指斥。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng also said: "The earlier words are still subtle—one should point and reproach more directly."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng added, "That was still too subtle. Press the attack more plainly."

sentences.zh: 愔應聲曰：「魏收在並作一篇詩，對眾讀訖，云：'打從叔季景出六百斗米，亦不辨此。

translations.literal: Yang Yan responded immediately: "Wei Shou at Bing composed a poem; after reading it before the crowd he said: 'Beat out six hundred dou of grain from clansman uncle Ji Jing—yet he does not recognize this.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan answered at once, "At Bing, Wei Shou wrote a poem and, after reading it aloud before the company, said, 'Beat six hundred dou of grain out of my clansman uncle Ji Jing—and still he does not recognize this.'

sentences.zh: '遠近所知，非敢妄說。」

translations.literal: It is known near and far—not daring to speak falsely."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone near and far knows it. I would not say so without cause."

sentences.zh: 文襄喜曰：「我亦先聞。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng said delightedly: "I too heard it first."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said with pleasure, "I heard that one too."

sentences.zh: 眾人皆笑。

translations.literal: All present laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed.

sentences.zh: 收雖自申雪，不復抗拒，終身病之。

translations.literal: Shou, though he cleared himself, no longer resisted; he bore the grievance for life.
translations.idiomatic: Shou tried to defend himself, but did not press the matter further, and carried the wound for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 侯景叛入梁，寇南境。

translations.literal: Hou Jing rebelled and entered Liang, raiding the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing rebelled, fled into Liang territory, and raided the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 文襄時在晉陽，令收為檄五十餘紙，不日而就。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng was then at Jinyang; he ordered Shou to draft over fifty proclamations; they were finished within days.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was then at Jinyang and ordered Shou to draft more than fifty proclamations. They were finished within days.

sentences.zh: 又檄梁朝，令送侯景，初夜執筆，三更便了，文過七紙。

translations.literal: He also sent a proclamation to Liang demanding the surrender of Hou Jing; Shou took up the brush at the first watch of the night and finished by the third watch—the text exceeded seven sheets.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted a proclamation to Liang demanding Hou Jing's surrender. Shou began writing at the first watch of the night and finished by the third, producing more than seven sheets of text.

sentences.zh: 文襄善之。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 魏帝曾委秋大射，普令賦詩，收詩末云：「尺書征建鄴，折簡召長安。」

translations.literal: The Wei emperor once held autumn grand archery and universally ordered poems; at the end of Shou's poem it said: "A foot-long letter summons Jiankang; a folded slip calls Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor once held the autumn grand archery ceremony and ordered everyone to compose poems. At the end of Shou's poem came the lines, "A brief letter summons Jiankang; a folded note calls Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 文襄壯之，顧謂人曰：「在朝今有魏收，便是國之光采。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng admired it; turning, he said to those present: "In court today, having Wei Shou is the nation's glory.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng was stirred by it and, turning to those around him, said, "With Wei Shou in court today, the state has its ornament.

sentences.zh: 雅俗文墨，通達縱橫。

translations.literal: Refined and vulgar, writing and ink—penetrating all, reaching everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He moves with equal ease through refined and plain styles, through every kind of writing.

sentences.zh: 我亦使子才、子升，時有所作，至於詞氣，並不及之。

translations.literal: I also have Zicai and Zisheng compose at times; as for diction and spirit, none compare to him.
translations.idiomatic: I have Zicai and Zisheng write from time to time as well, but in force of language none of them equals him.

sentences.zh: 吾或決有所懷，忘而不語，語而不盡，意有未及，收呈草，皆以周悉。

translations.literal: When I sometimes decide on something in mind, forget and do not speak, speak but not completely, meaning not fully reached—Shou presents drafts and all are thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When I have made up my mind but forget to say it, or say it but not fully, or leave something unsaid, Shou's drafts always say everything that needed saying.

sentences.zh: 此亦難有。」

translations.literal: This too is hard to find."
translations.idiomatic: That is rare indeed."

sentences.zh: 又敕兼主客郎，接梁使謝珽、徐陵。

translations.literal: He also ordered him additionally to serve as Master of Guests, receiving the Liang envoys Xie Yue and Xu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Shou to serve additionally as Master of Guests and receive the Liang envoys Xie Yue and Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 侯景既陷梁，梁鄱陽王范時為合州刺史，文襄敕收以書喻之。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing had overrun Liang, the Liang Prince of Poyang, Fan, was then governor of He Province; Gao Cheng ordered Shou to persuade him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing had overrun Liang, Prince Fan of Poyang was serving as governor of He Province. Gao Cheng ordered Shou to write and persuade him.

sentences.zh: 范得書，仍率部伍西上，州刺史崔聖念入據其城。

translations.literal: Fan received the letter and still led his troops west; the provincial governor Cui Shengian entered and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan received the letter and marched west with his forces, while the provincial governor Cui Shengian entered and took the city.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂收曰：「今定一州，卿有其力，猶恨'尺書征建鄴'未效耳。」

translations.literal: Gao Cheng said to Shou: "Now that a province is secured, you had a hand in it—yet I still regret that 'a foot-long letter summons Jiankang' has not yet taken effect."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng said to Shou, "We have secured a province today, and you had a hand in it. All the same, I still regret that your line about summoning Jiankang with a brief letter has not yet come true."

sentences.zh: 文襄崩，文宣如晉陽，令與黃門郎崔季舒、高德正、吏部郎中尉瑾于北第參掌機密。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng died; Gao Yang went to Jinyang and ordered him, together with Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Jishu, Gao Dezheng, and Bureau Director Wei Jin, to manage secrets at the Northern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Cheng died, Gao Yang went to Jinyang and ordered Shou, together with Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Jishu, Gao Dezheng, and Bureau Director Wei Jin, to handle confidential affairs at the Northern Residence.

sentences.zh: 轉秘書監，兼著作郎，又除定州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, concurrently served as Compiler, and was also appointed Chief Rectifier of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, continued as Compiler, and was also appointed Chief Rectifier of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 時齊將受禪，楊愔奏收置之別館，令撰禪代詔冊諸文，遣徐之才守門，不聽出。

translations.literal: When Qi was about to receive the abdication, Yang Kai memorialized to place Shou in a separate lodge, order him to compose the abdication edicts, proclamations, and related documents, and sent Xu Zhicai to guard the door, not allowing him out.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was about to receive the abdication, Yang Kai memorialized that Shou be lodged separately and ordered to draft the abdication edicts and related documents. Xu Zhicai was sent to guard the door and keep him from leaving.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，除中書令，仍兼著作郎，封富平縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, still concurrently served as Compiler, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, continued as Compiler, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fuping County.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔撰魏史。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered the compilation of the Wei History.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict ordered the compilation of the History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 四年，除魏尹，故優以祿力，專在史閣，不知郡事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Mayor of the Wei Capital; therefore he was given preferential salary and resources, devoted exclusively to the History Office, and unaware of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Mayor of the Wei Capital, but was given preferential salary and support so that he could devote himself entirely to the History Office and leave prefectural affairs alone.

sentences.zh: 初，帝令群臣各言志，收曰：「臣願得直筆東觀，早出魏書。」

translations.literal: Initially, the emperor ordered the officials each to state their aspiration; Shou said: "Your servant wishes to wield the straight brush at the Eastern Pavilion and produce the Wei History early."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had ordered each official to declare his ambition. Shou said, "Your servant wishes to wield an honest brush at the Eastern Pavilion and finish the History of Wei soon."

sentences.zh: 故帝使收專其任。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor had Shou exclusively carry this charge.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason the emperor put Shou in sole charge of the task.

sentences.zh: 又詔平原王高隆之總監之，署名而已。

translations.literal: An edict also appointed Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi to supervise it—in name only, signing his name.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also named Prince Gao Longzhi of Pingyuan as general supervisor, though in practice he only affixed his name.

sentences.zh: 帝敕收曰：「好直筆，我終不作魏太武誅史官。」

translations.literal: The emperor charged Shou, saying: "Write straight—I will never be like Emperor Taiwu of Wei, who killed historiographers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Shou, "Write honestly. I will never do what Emperor Taiwu of Wei did and kill the historiographers."

sentences.zh: 始，魏初鄧彥海撰代記十餘卷，其後崔浩典史，游雅、高允、程駿、李彪、崔光、李琰之郎知世修其業。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in early Wei Deng Yanhai compiled the Dynastic Record in over ten scrolls; afterward Cui Hao managed the history; You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yanzhi, and others through generations maintained the work.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, in early Wei, Deng Yanhai compiled the Dynastic Record in more than ten scrolls. Later Cui Hao took charge of the history, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, Li Yanzhi, and others carried on the work through successive generations.

sentences.zh: 浩為編年體，彪始分作紀、表、志、傳，書猶未出。

translations.literal: Hao used the annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies—the book still had not been published.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote in annalistic form; Biao was the first to divide the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the book had still not appeared.

sentences.zh: 宜武時，命邢巒追撰孝文起居注，書至太和十四年。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time, Xing Luan was ordered to continue compiling Emperor Xiaowen's Daily Records; the book reached the fourteenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu, Xing Luan was ordered to continue compiling Emperor Xiaowen's Daily Records, bringing the account down to the fourteenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 又命崔鴻、王遵業補續焉，下訖孝明，事甚委悉。

translations.literal: Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were also ordered to supplement and continue it, down to Emperor Xiaoming—the matters were very detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were then ordered to supplement and continue it down to Emperor Xiaoming, in very full detail.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王暉業撰辨宗室錄三十卷。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiyin Hui Ye compiled the Record for Identifying the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui Ye of Jiyin compiled the Record for Identifying the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 收於是與通直常侍房延佑、司空司馬辛元植、國子博士刁柔、裴昂之、尚書郎高孝幹專總斟酌，以成魏書。

translations.literal: Shou then, together with Regular Attendant Fang Yanyou, Minister of Works Secretary Xin Yuanzhi, National University Doctor Diao Rou, Pei Angzhi, and Secretariat Gentleman Gao Xiaogan, exclusively deliberated and weighed matters to complete the Wei History.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then worked with Regular Attendant Fang Yanyou, Minister of Works Secretary Xin Yuanzhi, National University Doctor Diao Rou, Pei Angzhi, and Secretariat Gentleman Gao Xiaogan to weigh and organize the material and complete the History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 辯定名稱，隨條甄舉。

translations.literal: They clarified and fixed names, selecting according to each category.
translations.idiomatic: They settled names and titles and selected entries category by category.

sentences.zh: 又搜采亡遺，綴續後事，備一代史籍，表而上聞之。

translations.literal: They also searched and collected lost material, appended later events, completed the historical records of one dynasty, and memorialized and submitted them upward.
translations.idiomatic: They also gathered lost records, appended later events, and assembled a complete history of the dynasty, which they memorialized and submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 勒成一代大典：凡十二紀，九十二列傳，合一百一十卷。

translations.literal: They forged the great canon of one dynasty: twelve annals, ninety-two biographies, totaling one hundred ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The finished canon of the dynasty comprised twelve annals and ninety-two biographies, one hundred ten scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，奏上之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, they memorialized and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year it was memorialized and submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋，除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, he was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 收以志未成，奏請終業，許之。

translations.literal: Shou, because the treatises were not yet complete, memorialized requesting to finish the work; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, because the treatises were still unfinished, memorialized asking leave to complete them, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一月復奏十志：天象四卷，地形三卷，律曆二卷，禮樂四卷，食貨一卷，刑罰一卷，靈徵二卷，官氏二卷，釋老一卷，凡二十卷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he again submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena four scrolls, Geography three scrolls, Calendars and Chronology two scrolls, Rites and Music four scrolls, Food and Currency one scroll, Punishments one scroll, Portents two scrolls, Offices and Clans two scrolls, Buddhism and Daoism one scroll—twenty scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he submitted the ten treatises again: Celestial Phenomena in four scrolls, Geography in three, Calendars and Chronology in two, Rites and Music in four, Food and Currency in one, Punishments in one, Portents in two, Offices and Clans in two, and Buddhism and Daoism in one—twenty scrolls altogether.

sentences.zh: 續于紀傳，合一百三十卷。

translations.literal: Continued with the annals and biographies, totaling one hundred thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Added to the annals and biographies, the work came to one hundred thirty scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 分為十二表，其史三十五例，二十五序，九十四論，前後二表一啟，皆獨出於收。

translations.literal: It was divided into twelve tables; the history had thirty-five principles, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, two memorials and one report at beginning and end—all solely from Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The work was divided into twelve tables. Its thirty-five principles, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and the two memorials and one report at the beginning and end were all Wei Shou's work alone.

sentences.zh: 收所引史官，恐其陵逼，唯取學流先相依附者。

translations.literal: The history officials Shou employed—fearing they might overreach him—he took only those from the scholarly community who had long been dependent on him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the history officials Wei Shou enlisted, fearing they might overbear him, he chose only scholars who had long relied on him.

sentences.zh: 其房延祐、辛元植、眭仲讓雖夙涉朝位，並非史才；

translations.literal: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang, though long involved in court rank, were none of them suited for history;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanyou, Xin Yuanzhi, and Sui Zhongrang had long held court office, yet none possessed the talent for history;

sentences.zh: 刁柔、裴昂之以儒業見知，全不堪編緝；

translations.literal: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were known for Confucian learning, yet were wholly unfit for compilation;
translations.idiomatic: Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi were esteemed for Confucian scholarship but were altogether unfit for editorial work;

sentences.zh: 高孝幹以左道求進。

translations.literal: Gao Xiaogan sought advancement through heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaogan sought promotion through unorthodox methods.

sentences.zh: 修史諸人，宗祖姻戚，多被書錄，飾以美言。

translations.literal: The kin and affinal relatives of those who compiled the history were widely recorded and adorned with fine words.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors and in-laws of those who worked on the history were widely entered in the record and dressed up in flattering language.

sentences.zh: 收頗急，不甚能平，夙有怨者，多沒其善。

translations.literal: Shou was rather quick-tempered and not very even-handed; those with old grievances often had their virtues suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was quick-tempered and not very fair-minded; those who had long borne him a grudge often found their good deeds omitted.

sentences.zh: 每言：「何物小子，敢共魏收作色！

translations.literal: He often said: "What sort of whelp dares show defiance toward Wei Shou!
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "What kind of stripling dares stand up to Wei Shou!

sentences.zh: 舉之則使上天，按之當使入地。」

translations.literal: Raise him and I can send him to heaven; press him down and I can send him to earth."
translations.idiomatic: Lift him up and I can raise him to heaven; press him down and I can drive him into the ground."

sentences.zh: 初，收在神武時為太常少卿，修國史，得陽休之助。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Gao Huan's time, Shou served as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, compiled the national history, and received Yang Xiuzhi's assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Gao Huan, Wei Shou had served as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and compiled the national history with Yang Xiuzhi's help.

sentences.zh: 因謝休之曰：「無以謝德，當為卿作佳傳。」

translations.literal: He therefore thanked Xiuzhi, saying: "I have no way to repay your kindness; I shall write you an excellent biography."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore thanked Xiuzhi, saying, "I have no adequate way to repay your kindness; I shall write you a fine biography."

sentences.zh: 休之父固，魏世為北平太守，以貪虐為中尉李平所彈獲罪，載在魏起居注。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's father Gu, in Wei times served as Governor of Beiping; for greed and cruelty he was impeached and convicted by Chief Commandant Li Ping, as recorded in the Wei Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's father Gu had served as Governor of Beiping under Wei. He was impeached and convicted by Chief Commandant Li Ping for greed and cruelty, a fact recorded in the Wei Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 收書云：「固為北平，甚有惠政，坐公事免官。」

translations.literal: In Shou's book it says: "Gu governed Beiping with great benevolent administration and was dismissed from office on official business."
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Shou's history it says, "Gu governed Beiping with notable benevolence and was removed from office on official grounds."

sentences.zh: 又云：「李平深相敬重。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Li Ping deeply respected him."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Li Ping held him in deep esteem."

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮于魏為賊，收以高氏出自爾硃，且納榮子金，故減其惡而增其善，論云：「若修德義之風，同韓、彭、伊、霍，夫何足數。」

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong was a rebel against Wei; Shou, because the Gao clan traced its origin to Erzhu and because he accepted gold from Rong's son, reduced his evils and increased his virtues, writing in a disquisition: "If one cultivated the wind of virtue and righteousness, ranking with Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang, what would be worth counting?"
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong had been a rebel against Wei. Because the Gao clan traced its descent to the Erzhu line and because Wei Shou had accepted gold from Rong's son, he softened Rong's crimes and magnified his virtues, writing in a disquisition, "If one cultivated virtue and righteousness, standing with Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang, what would there be to reckon?"

sentences.zh: 時論既言收著史不平，文宣詔收于尚書省與諸家子孫共加論討。

translations.literal: Public opinion having said Shou's history was unfair, Gao Yang ordered Shou at the Ministry of State Affairs to discuss and review it jointly with descendants of the various families.
translations.idiomatic: Once public opinion declared that Wei Shou's history was biased, Gao Yang ordered him to the Ministry of State Affairs to review it together with descendants of the affected families.

sentences.zh: 前後投訴，百有餘人，雲遺其世職位；

translations.literal: More than a hundred people filed complaints before and after, saying their hereditary offices had been omitted;
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred people lodged complaints, saying their families' hereditary offices had been left out;

sentences.zh: 或云其家不見記錄；

translations.literal: or that their families had not been recorded;
translations.idiomatic: or that their families had not been entered in the history at all;

sentences.zh: 或云妄有非毀。

translations.literal: or that there had been groundless slander.
translations.idiomatic: or that they had been slandered without cause.

sentences.zh: 收皆隨狀答之，

translations.literal: Shou answered each according to the particulars.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou answered each complaint according to its particulars.

sentences.zh: 范陽盧斐父同附出族祖玄傳下；

translations.literal: Lu Fei of Fanyang's father Tong was attached under the biography of his clan forebear Lu Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fei of Fanyang's father Tong had been appended under the biography of his clan forebear Lu Xuan;

sentences.zh: 頓丘李庶家傳，稱其本是梁國家人。

translations.literal: In Li Shu's family biography of Dunqiu, it said his family were originally retainers of the state of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Shu's family record from Dunqiu, it was said that his family had originally been household retainers of Liang.

sentences.zh: 斐、庶譏議，雲史書不直。

translations.literal: Fei and Shu criticized, saying the history was not truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Fei and Shu attacked the work, declaring that the history was not truthful.

sentences.zh: 收性急，不勝其憤，啟誣其欲加屠害。

translations.literal: Shou, by nature impatient, unable to bear his anger, memorialized falsely accusing them of intending to slaughter him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, quick-tempered by nature and unable to contain his rage, memorialized falsely accusing them of plotting to kill him.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，親自詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and personally interrogated and rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and personally cross-examined and rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 斐曰：「臣父仕魏。

translations.literal: Fei said: "My father served Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "My father served Wei.

sentences.zh: 位至儀同，功業顯著，名聞天下，與收無親，遂不立傳。

translations.literal: He rose to the rank of Grand Equal-in-Attendance; his achievements were outstanding and his name known throughout the realm; he had no kinship with Shou, yet no biography was made for him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of Grand Equal-in-Attendance, his achievements were distinguished and his name known throughout the realm, yet though he had no kinship with Wei Shou, no biography was written for him.

sentences.zh: 博陵崔綽，位至本郡功曹，更無事蹟，是收外親，乃為傳首。」

translations.literal: Cui Chuo of Boling reached only the rank of Merit Officer in his native commandery and had no further accomplishments; he was Shou's affinal relative, yet was placed at the head of a biography."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chuo of Boling had risen only to Merit Officer in his home commandery and had no further achievements to his name, yet as Wei Shou's affinal kinsman he was made the lead subject of a biography."

sentences.zh: 收曰：「綽雖無位，道義可嘉，所以合傳。」

translations.literal: Shou said: "Though Chuo had no lofty rank, his moral conduct was admirable, and so he was included in a combined biography."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "Though Chuo held no high office, his moral conduct was admirable, and so he was included in a combined biography."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿何由知其好人？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How do you know he was a good man?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How do you know he was a good man?"

sentences.zh: 收曰：「高允曾為綽贊，稱有道德。」

translations.literal: Shou said: "Gao Yun once wrote a eulogy for Chuo, praising his moral virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "Gao Yun once composed a eulogy for Chuo, praising his moral character."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「司空才士，為人作贊，正應稱揚。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Minister of Works was a man of talent; when writing a eulogy for someone, of course he would speak praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Minister of Works was a man of talent; when he wrote a eulogy for someone, of course he would speak in praise.

sentences.zh: 亦如卿為人作文章，道其好者，豈能皆實？」

translations.literal: It is just as when you write for others and speak of their good qualities—can it all be true?"
translations.idiomatic: It is the same as when you write for others and speak of their virtues—can it all be true?"

sentences.zh: 收無以對，戰慄而已。

translations.literal: Shou had no reply and could only tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou had no answer and could only tremble.

sentences.zh: 但帝先重收才，不欲加罪。

translations.literal: But the emperor had long valued Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor had long valued Wei Shou's talent and did not wish to punish him.

sentences.zh: 時太原王松年亦謗史，及斐、庶並獲罪，各被鞭配甲坊，或因以致死。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Songnian of Taiyuan also slandered the history; he, Fei, and Shu were all convicted, each flogged and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died as a result.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Songnian of Taiyuan also attacked the history. He, Fei, and Shu were all convicted, flogged, and assigned to the armorers' ward, and some died from it.

sentences.zh: 盧思道亦抵罪。

translations.literal: Lu Sidao was also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sidao was punished as well.

sentences.zh: 然猶以群口沸騰，敕魏史且勿施行，令群官博議。

translations.literal: Still, because public voices seethed, he ordered that the Wei History not yet be promulgated and directed officials to debate it broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Still, because public opinion continued to boil over, he ordered that the Wei History not be promulgated for the time being and directed the officials to debate it at length.

sentences.zh: 聽有家事者入署，不實者陳牒。

translations.literal: Those with family matters at stake were permitted to enter the office; any inaccuracies they could file memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Those with family interests at stake were allowed to enter the office, and anyone who found inaccuracies could submit a memorial.

sentences.zh: 於是眾口喧然，號為「穢史」，投牒者相次，收無以抗之。

translations.literal: Then voices clamored, calling it the "Filthy History"; memorial filers came one after another, and Shou could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Then voices rose in uproar, calling it the "Filthy History." Memorials poured in one after another, and Wei Shou could not hold out against them.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射楊愔、右僕射高德正二人勢傾朝野，與收皆親。

translations.literal: At the time the Left Vice Director Yang Yin and Right Vice Director Gao Dezheng—the two men whose power tilted court and countryside—were both close to Shou.
