translations.idiomatic: At the time the Left Vice Director Yang Yin and the Right Vice Director Gao Dezheng, whose power dominated court and countryside alike, were both on intimate terms with Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 收遂為其家並作傳，二人不欲言史不實，抑塞拆辭，終文宣世，更不重論。

translations.literal: Shou thereupon wrote biographies for both their families; the two men did not wish to say the history was untrue, suppressed and dismantled the arguments, and throughout Gao Yang's reign it was never debated again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou then wrote biographies for both their families. Unwilling to say the history was false, the two men suppressed and picked apart the complaints, and throughout Gao Yang's reign the matter was never reopened.

sentences.zh: 又尚書陸操嘗謂愔曰：「魏收魏書可謂博物宏才，有大功于魏室。」

translations.literal: Also, the Minister Lu Cao once said to Yin: "Wei Shou's Book of Wei may be called learned and grand in talent, a great service to the Wei house."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Lu Cao once said to Yang Yin, "Wei Shou's Book of Wei is a work of broad learning and great talent, a major service to the house of Wei."

sentences.zh: 愔嘗謂收曰：「此謂不刊之書，傳之萬古。

translations.literal: Yin once said to Shou: "This is what is called an irrevocable book, to be transmitted for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin once told Wei Shou, "This is what people call an irrevocable book, one to be handed down for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 但恨論及諸家枝葉親姻，過為繁碎，與舊史體例不同耳。」

translations.literal: I only regret that in treating the branches, leaves, and affinal kin of the various families it is excessively detailed and trivial, unlike the format of earlier histories."
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that in treating the branches, collateral lines, and affinal kin of the various families it is excessively detailed, unlike the format of earlier histories."

sentences.zh: 收曰：「往因中原喪亂，人士譜牒遺逸略盡，是以具盡其枝派。

translations.literal: Shou said: "Formerly, because of the disorder and ruin in the Central Plains, gentlemen's genealogical records were largely lost, and so I fully set forth all their branches.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "In the past, because of the chaos and ruin in the Central Plains, gentlemen's genealogical records were largely lost, and so I set forth their branches in full.

sentences.zh: 望公觀過知仁，以免尤責。」

translations.literal: I hope you will see my intent through my fault and spare me severe blame."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will read my intent through my fault and spare me harsh censure."

sentences.zh: 八年夏，除太子少傅，監國史。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 復參修律令。

translations.literal: He again participated in revising statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in revising statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 三台成，文宣曰：「台成，須有賦。」

translations.literal: When the Three Terraces were completed, Gao Yang said: "The terraces are complete; there must be a rhapsody."
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Terraces were completed, Gao Yang said, "The terraces are finished; there must be a rhapsody."

sentences.zh: 愔先以告收，收上《皇居新殿台賦》，其文甚壯麗。

translations.literal: Yin first informed Shou; Shou submitted the "Rhapsody on the New Palatial Terraces of the Imperial Residence," its prose very bold and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin told Wei Shou beforehand, and Shou submitted his "Rhapsody on the New Palatial Terraces of the Imperial Residence," a piece of writing bold and splendid in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 時所作者自邢邵已下，咸不逮焉。

translations.literal: Among those who composed at the time, from Xing Shao downward, none matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who wrote at the time, from Xing Shao on down, none could equal it.

sentences.zh: 收上賦前數日，乃告邢邵，邵後告人曰：「收甚惡人，不早言之。」

translations.literal: A few days before Shou submitted his rhapsody he only then told Xing Shao; Shao later told others: "Shou is a vile fellow—not telling me sooner."
translations.idiomatic: Only a few days before submitting his rhapsody did Wei Shou tell Xing Shao. Shao later said to others, "Shou is a contemptible man—not telling me sooner."

sentences.zh: 帝曾遊東山，敕收作詔，宣揚威德，譬喻關西。

translations.literal: The emperor once toured the Eastern Hills and ordered Shou to draft an edict proclaiming his might and virtue, with metaphors about the western passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once toured the Eastern Hills and ordered Wei Shou to draft an edict proclaiming imperial might and virtue, with pointed metaphors about the western passes.

sentences.zh: 俄頃而訖，辭理宏壯，帝對百僚大嗟賞之。

translations.literal: In no time it was finished; its logic and language were grand and bold, and before the hundred officials the emperor greatly admired and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: In no time it was finished, its argument and language grand and forceful. Before the assembled officials the emperor admired and praised it at length.

sentences.zh: 仍兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: He continued concurrently as Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to serve concurrently as Grand Steward of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 收娶其舅女，崔昂之妹，產一女，無子。

translations.literal: Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, the sister of Cui Angzhi; she bore one daughter; there were no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou married his maternal uncle's daughter, the sister of Cui Angzhi. She bore one daughter, but there were no sons.

sentences.zh: 魏太常劉芳孫女、中書郎崔肇師女，夫家坐事，帝並賜收為妻。

translations.literal: The granddaughters of Wei Director of the Ancestral Temple Liu Fang and Secretariat Gentleman Cui Zhaoshi—their husbands' families having been implicated in crimes—the emperor bestowed both on Shou as wives.
translations.idiomatic: The granddaughters of Liu Fang, Director of the Ancestral Temple under Wei, and of Secretariat Gentleman Cui Zhaoshi, whose husbands' families had been implicated in crimes, the emperor bestowed on Wei Shou as wives.

sentences.zh: 時人比之賈充置左右夫人。

translations.literal: People of the time compared this to Jia Chong's establishment of two consorts, one on each side.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared this to Jia Chong's arrangement of consorts on his left and right.

sentences.zh: 然無子。

translations.literal: Yet there were no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still had no sons.

sentences.zh: 後病甚，恐身後嫡媵不平，乃放二姬。

translations.literal: Later, when gravely ill, fearing discord between primary wife and concubines after his death, he released the two secondary wives.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he fell gravely ill, fearing strife between his principal wife and concubines after his death, he released his two secondary wives.

sentences.zh: 及疾瘳追憶，作《懷離賦》以申意。

translations.literal: When he recovered from illness he recalled them with longing and composed the "Rhapsody on Cherishing Separation" to express his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered and looked back with longing, he composed the "Rhapsody on Cherishing Separation" to give voice to his feelings.

sentences.zh: 文宣每以酣宴之次，雲太子性懦，宗社事重，終當傳位常山。

translations.literal: Gao Yang, at the height of revelry, would say the Crown Prince was timid by nature, that affairs of state and altar were weighty, and that the throne would ultimately pass to the Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his revels Gao Yang would say that the Crown Prince was timid by nature, that the fate of state and altar was weighty, and that the throne would ultimately pass to the Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 收謂楊愔曰：「古人云：太子國之根本，不可動搖。

translations.literal: Shou said to Yang Yin: "The ancients said: 'The Crown Prince is the root of the state and must not be shaken.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said to Yang Yin, "The ancients said, 'The Crown Prince is the root of the state and must not be shaken.'

sentences.zh: 至尊三爵後，每言傳位常山，令臣下疑貳。

translations.literal: After His Majesty has drunk three cups, he repeatedly speaks of passing the throne to Changshan, leaving the ministers divided in mind.
translations.idiomatic: After His Majesty has drunk three rounds, he repeatedly speaks of passing the throne to Changshan, leaving his ministers divided and uncertain.

sentences.zh: 若實，便須決行；

translations.literal: If this is real, it must be carried out decisively;
translations.idiomatic: If he means it, the transfer must be carried out decisively;

sentences.zh: 若戲此言，魏收既忝師傅，正當守之以死，但恐國家不安。」

translations.literal: if these words are jest, Wei Shou, having the dishonor of being tutor, ought to defend the heir even unto death, though I fear the realm will not be secure."
translations.idiomatic: if these words are only jest, then Wei Shou, unworthy though he is as tutor, ought to defend the heir even unto death—yet I fear the realm will not be secure."

sentences.zh: 愔以收言奏帝，自此便止。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin reported Wei Shou's words to the emperor, and from then on Gao Yang stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝數宴喜，收每預侍從。

translations.literal: The emperor frequently held feasts and celebrations; Shou always attended in service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often held feasts and celebrations, and Wei Shou was always among those in attendance.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之納鄭良娣也，有司備設牢饌。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince took Lady Zheng as a secondary consort, the relevant offices prepared sacrificial feast provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince took Lady Zheng as a secondary consort, the relevant offices prepared a full sacrificial feast.

sentences.zh: 帝既酣飲，起而自毀覆之，仍詔收曰：「知我意不？」

translations.literal: The emperor, already deep in drink, rose and overturned them himself, then said to Shou: "Do you understand my intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Already deep in drink, the emperor rose and overturned the feast himself, then said to Wei Shou, "Do you understand what I mean?"

sentences.zh: 收曰：「臣愚謂良娣既東宮之妾，理不須牢，仰惟聖懷，緣此毀去。」

translations.literal: Shou said: "This foolish subject thinks that since Lady Liangdi is a concubine of the Eastern Palace, sacrificial feast provisions are not properly required; reverently pondering Your Majesty's mind, you overturned them for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "This foolish subject thinks that since Lady Liangdi is a concubine of the Eastern Palace, a full sacrificial feast is not properly required. Reverently pondering Your Majesty's intent, you overturned it for that reason."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，握收手曰：「卿知我意。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly, took Shou's hand, and said: "You understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily, took Wei Shou's hand, and said, "You understand me."

sentences.zh: 安德王延宗納趙郡李祖收女為刀，後帝幸李宅宴，而妃母宋氏薦二石榴於帝前。

translations.literal: Prince Andrade Yan Zong took the daughter of Li Zushou of Zhao commandery as a concubine; later the emperor visited the Li residence for a banquet, and the consort's mother Lady Song presented two pomegranates before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan Zong of Andre took the daughter of Li Zushou of Zhao commandery as a concubine. Later, when the emperor visited the Li residence for a banquet, the consort's mother, Lady Song, presented two pomegranates before him.

sentences.zh: 問諸人，莫知其意，帝投之。

translations.literal: He asked everyone; none knew the meaning, and the emperor threw them away.
translations.idiomatic: He asked those present, but none understood the meaning, and the emperor cast the fruit aside.

sentences.zh: 收曰：「石榴房中多子，王新婚，妃母欲子孫眾多。」

translations.literal: Shou said: "Pomegranates have many seeds within; the prince has newly married—the consort's mother wishes for many descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "Pomegranates are full of seeds within. The prince has just married, and the consort's mother wishes for many descendants."

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，詔收：「卿還將來。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered Shou: "Go back and bring them again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered Wei Shou, "Go back and bring them again."

sentences.zh: 仍賜收美錦二疋。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Shou two bolts of fine brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed on Wei Shou two bolts of fine brocade.

sentences.zh: 十年，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Grand Equal-in-Attendance, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Grand Equal-in-Attendance of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 帝在宴席，口敕以為中書監，命中書郎李愔以收一代盛才，難於率爾，久而未訖。

translations.literal: At a banquet the emperor orally ordered him made Director of the Secretariat; he charged Secretariat Gentleman Li Yin, because Shou was a supreme talent of his generation and the appointment could not be drafted casually, to write it—but it was long unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the emperor orally ordered that he be made Director of the Secretariat and charged Secretariat Gentleman Li Yin with drafting the appointment. Because Wei Shou was a supreme talent of his generation, the wording could not be dashed off casually, and the draft was long in coming.

sentences.zh: 比成，帝已醉醒，遂不重言，愔仍不奏，事竟寢。

translations.literal: By the time it was finished the emperor had drunk himself sober and did not mention it again; Yin still did not memorialize it, and the matter was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: By the time it was finished the emperor had drunk himself sober and did not mention it again. Li Yin still did not memorialize it, and the matter was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩于晉陽，驛召收及中山太守陽休之參議吉凶之禮，並掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Shou and Yang Xiuzhi, Governor of Zhongshan, to consult on rites of fortune and misfortune, and both managed edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jinyang, couriers summoned Wei Shou and Yang Xiuzhi, Governor of Zhongshan, to consult on the rites of mourning and celebration, and both were put in charge of edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 仍除侍中，遷太常卿，文宣諡及廟號、陵名，皆收議也。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and promoted to Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Gao Yang's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Shou's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and promoted to Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Gao Yang's posthumous title, temple name, and tomb name were all Wei Shou's work.

sentences.zh: 及孝昭居中宰事，命收禁中為諸詔文，積日不出。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao resided within and administered affairs, he ordered Shou to remain in the palace to compose various edict texts, and Shou did not leave for several days.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao governed from within the palace, he ordered Wei Shou to remain inside drafting edicts, and for several days Shou did not come out.

sentences.zh: 轉中書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，除兼侍中、右光祿大夫，仍儀同，監史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian, he was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, continued as Equal-in-Attendance, and supervised the history.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, retained his Equal-in-Attendance rank, and supervised the history project.

sentences.zh: 收先副王昕使梁，不相協睦，時昕弟晞親密，而孝昭別令休之兼中書，在晉陽典誥詔，收留在鄴，蓋晞所為。

translations.literal: Earlier Shou had served as Wang Xin's deputy on a mission to Liang, and the two had not been harmonious. At the time Xin's younger brother Xi was intimate with the ruler, and Xiaozhao separately ordered Xiuzhi to act concurrently in the Secretariat and handle proclamations and edicts at Jinyang, while Shou was left in Ye; this was presumably Xi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Shou had accompanied Wang Xin as deputy envoy to Liang, and the two had not gotten along. Since Xin's younger brother Xi was then close to the ruler, Xiaozhao separately ordered Xiuzhi to serve concurrently in the Secretariat and handle proclamations and edicts at Jinyang, while Wei Shou was left in Ye, presumably through Xi's influence.

sentences.zh: 收大不平，謂太子舍人盧詢祖：「若使卿作文誥，我亦不言。」

translations.literal: Shou was greatly aggrieved and said to Crown Prince Retainer Lu Xunzu, "If they had made you compose the documents and proclamations, I too would say nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was deeply resentful and told Crown Prince Retainer Lu Xunzu, "If they had made you draft the documents and proclamations, I would have said nothing."

sentences.zh: 又除祖珽為著作郎，欲以代收。

translations.literal: They also appointed Zu Ting as Gentleman Author, wishing to use him to replace Shou.
translations.idiomatic: They also appointed Zu Ting as Gentleman Author, intending him to replace Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 司空主簿李翥，文詞士也，聞而告人曰：「詔誥悉歸陽子烈，著作復遣祖孝征，文史頓失，恐魏公發背。」

translations.literal: Li Zhu, Registrar to the Minister of Works and a man of letters, heard this and told someone, "Edicts and proclamations have all gone to Yang Zilie, and for authorship they have again sent Zu Xiaozheng. Literature and history are suddenly lost; I fear Lord Wei will break out on his back."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhu, Registrar to the Minister of Works and a man of letters, heard of this and told others, "Edicts and proclamations have all gone to Yang Zilie, and the authorship post has again been given to Zu Xiaozheng. Literature and history are suddenly lost; I fear Lord Wei will develop a boil on his back."

sentences.zh: 于時詔議二王三恪，收執王肅、杜預義，以元、司馬氏為二王，通曹備三恪。

translations.literal: At the time an edict called for discussion of the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests. Shou held to the interpretations of Wang Su and Du Yu, taking the Yuan and Sima houses as the Two Kings and including the Cao to complete the Three Honored Guests.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, an edict ordered discussion of the Two Kings and Three Honored Guests. Wei Shou followed the views of Wang Su and Du Yu, treating the Yuan and Sima houses as the Two Kings and adding the Cao house to complete the Three Honored Guests.

sentences.zh: 詔諸禮學之官皆執鄭玄五代之議。

translations.literal: The edicted ritual scholars all held to Zheng Xuan's theory of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual scholars consulted by edict all held to Zheng Xuan's theory of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 孝昭後姓元，議恪不欲廣及，故議從收。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao's empress had the surname Yuan, and in discussing the honored guests he did not wish the matter extended broadly; therefore the deliberation followed Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaozhao's empress bore the Yuan surname, he did not want the honored-guest discussion broadened too far, so the court followed Wei Shou's proposal.

sentences.zh: 又除兼太子少傅，解侍中。

translations.literal: He was also appointed concurrent Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and relieved as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed concurrent Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and relieved of his Palace Attendant post.

sentences.zh: 帝以魏史未行，詔收更加研審，收奉詔，頗有改正。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Wei History had not been promulgated, ordered Shou to investigate and review it further; Shou obeyed the edict and made considerable corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wei History had not yet been promulgated, the emperor ordered Wei Shou to examine it further. Shou obeyed the edict and made considerable corrections.

sentences.zh: 及詔行魏史，收以為直置秘閣，外人無由得見，於是命送一本付並省，一本付鄴下，任人寫之。

translations.literal: When the edict promulgated the Wei History, Shou considered that if it were placed directly in the Secret Archives outsiders would have no means to see it; he therefore ordered one copy sent to the capital secretariat and one to Ye, allowing anyone to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict promulgated the Wei History, Wei Shou felt that if it were placed directly in the Secret Archives outsiders would have no way to see it. He therefore ordered one copy sent to the capital secretariat and one to Ye, where anyone might copy it.

sentences.zh: 太甯元年，加開府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiping, he was granted the Grand Prefecture establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiping he was granted the Grand Prefecture establishment.

sentences.zh: 河清二年，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing, he served concurrently as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing he served concurrently as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時武成酣飲終日，朝事專委侍中高元海，凡庸不堪大任。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Wucheng drank himself through the day; court affairs were entrusted wholly to Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai, a mediocrity unfit for great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Wucheng drank through the day, entrusting court affairs wholly to Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai, a mediocrity unfit for great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 以收才名振俗，都官尚書畢義雲長於斷割，乃虛心倚仗。

translations.literal: Because Shou's literary reputation shook the age and Minister of Justice Bi Yiyun excelled at decisive judgment, the emperor leaned on them with an open mind.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei Shou's literary reputation dominated the age and Bi Yiyun, Minister of Justice, excelled at decisive judgment, the emperor leaned on them with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 收畏避，不能匡救，為議者所譏。

translations.literal: Shou shrank back in fear and could not rectify and rescue the situation; critics satirized him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou shrank back in fear and could not set things right, and critics satirized him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝于華林別起玄洲苑，備山水台觀之麗，詔於閣上畫收，其見重如此。

translations.literal: The emperor separately built the Xuanshou Garden at Hualin, complete with the splendor of mountains, waters, terraces, and pavilions, and ordered Shou painted on a pavilion—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor separately built the Xuanshou Garden at Hualin, complete with the splendor of mountains, waters, terraces, and pavilions, and ordered Wei Shou painted on a pavilion wall—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 始收比溫子升、邢邵稍為後進，邵既被疏出，子升以罪死，收遂大被任用，獨步一時。

translations.literal: At first Shou, compared with Wen Zisheng and Xing Shao, was somewhat the junior; after Shao was estranged and sent away and Zisheng died by crime, Shou was greatly employed and walked alone in his age.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei Shou, compared with Wen Zisheng and Xing Shao, had been somewhat the junior. After Shao was estranged and sent away and Zisheng died in disgrace, Shou came into great favor and stood alone in his age.

sentences.zh: 議論更相訾毀，各有朋黨。

translations.literal: In debate they slandered each other in turn, each with his own faction.
translations.idiomatic: In debate they slandered one another in turn, each with his own faction.

sentences.zh: 收每議陋邢文。

translations.literal: Shou always disparaged Xing's writing in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In discussion Wei Shou always belittled Xing Shao's writing.

sentences.zh: 邵又云：「江南任昉，文體本疏，魏收非直模擬，亦大偷竊。」

translations.literal: Shao also said: "Ren Fang of Jiangnan had a style inherently loose; Wei Shou not only imitates him but greatly plunders him as well."
translations.idiomatic: Shao also said, "Ren Fang of Jiangnan wrote in a style inherently loose. Wei Shou not only imitates him but plunders him wholesale."

sentences.zh: 收聞乃曰：「伊常于沈約集中作賊，何意道我偷任。」

translations.literal: When Shou heard this he said: "He is always a thief in Shen Yue's collected works—how dare he say I stole from Ren!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Shou heard this he said, "He is always plundering Shen Yue's collected works—how dare he say I stole from Ren Fang!"

sentences.zh: 任、沈俱有重名，邢、魏各有所好。

translations.literal: Ren and Shen both had heavy names; Xing and Wei each had what they favored.
translations.idiomatic: Both Ren Fang and Shen Yue enjoyed great fame; Xing Shao and Wei Shou each had his own preference.

sentences.zh: 武平中，黃門郎顏之推以二公意問僕射祖珽。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era, Yellow Gate Attendant Yan Zhitui asked Vice Director Zu Ting the views of the two lords.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era, Yellow Gate Attendant Yan Zhitui asked Vice Director Zu Ting what the two men thought.

sentences.zh: 珽答曰：「見邢、魏之臧不，即是任、沈之優劣。」

translations.literal: Ting replied: "Seeing whether Xing and Wei are good or bad is itself the relative merit of Ren and Shen."
translations.idiomatic: Ting replied, "To see whether Xing Shao and Wei Shou are good or bad is to see the relative merit of Ren Fang and Shen Yue."

sentences.zh: 收以溫子升全不作賦，邢雖有一兩首，又非所長，常云：「會須能作賦，始成大才士。

translations.literal: Shou [noted] that Wen Zisheng never wrote fu at all; though Xing had one or two pieces, they were not his forte. He often said: "One must be able to write fu before one can become a great man of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou held that Wen Zisheng never wrote fu at all, and that although Xing Shao had one or two pieces, they were not his strength. He often said, "Only one who can write fu deserves to be called a great man of letters.

sentences.zh: 唯以章表碑誌自許，此外更同兒戲。」

translations.literal: They pride themselves only on memorials, stele inscriptions, and epitaphs; beyond that everything else is the same as child's play."
translations.idiomatic: They pride themselves only on memorials, stele inscriptions, and epitaphs; everything else, to his mind, was child's play."

sentences.zh: 自武定二年以後，國家大事詔命，軍國文詞，皆收所作。

translations.literal: From the second year of Wuding onward, all major state edicts and proclamations and military and civil dispatches were written by Shou.
translations.idiomatic: From the second year of Wuding onward, every major state edict and proclamation and every military or civil dispatch was written by Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 每有警急，受詔立成。

translations.literal: Whenever there was urgent alarm, he received the edict and completed the piece on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was an emergency, he received the edict and finished the draft at once.

sentences.zh: 或時中使催促，收筆下有同宿構，敏速之工，邢、溫所不逮也。

translations.literal: Sometimes when palace envoys pressed him, what flowed from Shou's brush seemed pre-composed overnight—a speed and skill that Xing and Wen could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when palace envoys pressed him, what flowed from Wei Shou's brush seemed already composed overnight—a swiftness and mastery that neither Xing Shao nor Wen Zisheng could equal.

sentences.zh: 其參議典禮，與邢相埒。

translations.literal: In deliberating ritual propriety, he was equal to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In deliberating ritual propriety, he was the equal of Xing Shao.

sentences.zh: 既而趙郡公增年獲免，收知而過之，事發除名。

translations.literal: Later, Duke Zengnian of Zhao Commandery was able to escape punishment; Shou knew of it and let it pass, and when the matter came to light he was stripped of his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Duke Zengnian of Zhao Commandery escaped punishment. Wei Shou knew and let it pass; when the affair was exposed, he was removed from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 其年，又以托附陳使封孝琰，牒令其門客與行，遇昆侖舶至，得奇貨：猓然褥表、美玉盈尺等數十件。

translations.literal: That same year, he also entrusted himself to the Chen envoy Feng Xiaoyan and sent a document ordering his retainers to travel with him. When a Kunlun ship arrived, he obtained rare goods: a guoran rug-cover, fine jade a chi long, and several dozen other items.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he also attached himself to the Chen envoy Feng Xiaoyan, sending a document that ordered his retainers to accompany him. When a Kunlun ship arrived, he obtained rare goods, including a guoran rug-cover, fine jade a full chi long, and dozens of other items.

sentences.zh: 罪當流，以贖論。

translations.literal: The offense deserved exile, but it was judged redeemable by payment.
translations.idiomatic: The offense merited exile, but it was handled as redeemable by payment.

sentences.zh: 三年，起除清郡尹。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was restored and appointed Governor of Qing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was restored to office as Governor of Qing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋遣黃門郎元文遙敕收曰：「卿舊人，事我家最久，前者之罪，情在可恕。

translations.literal: Soon Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Wenyao was sent to issue an imperial message to Shou: "You are an old servant and have served my family longest. As for your earlier offense, the circumstances make it pardonable.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yellow Gate Gentleman Yuan Wenyao was sent to convey an imperial message to Wei Shou: "You are an old servant and have served my family longest. As for your earlier offense, the circumstances make it pardonable.

sentences.zh: 比令卿為尹，非謂美授，但初起卿，斟酌如此。

translations.literal: Recently making you governor was not what would be called a fine appointment; it was only because you were just being restored that the weighing was done this way.
translations.idiomatic: Recently making you governor was not a handsome appointment; it was only because you had just been restored that the matter was weighed this way.

sentences.zh: 朕豈可用卿之才而忘卿身？

translations.literal: How could I use your talent and forget your person?
translations.idiomatic: How could I use your talent yet forget the man himself?

sentences.zh: 待至十月，當還卿開府。」

translations.literal: Wait until the tenth month, and I shall restore you to Kaifu."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the tenth month, and I shall restore you to Kaifu."

sentences.zh: 天統元年，除左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiantong he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left.

sentences.zh: 二年，行齊州刺史，尋為真。

translations.literal: In the second year, he acted as Inspector of Qizhou and was soon made substantive.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he acted as Inspector of Qizhou and was soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 收以子侄年少，申以戒曆，著枕中篇。

translations.literal: Because his nephews and sons were young, Shou set forth admonitions drawn from the warnings of past ages and composed the Pillow Essay.
translations.idiomatic: Because his nephews were still young, Wei Shou set forth admonitions drawn from the lessons of past ages and wrote the Pillow Essay.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 吾曾覽管子之書，其言曰：「任之重者莫如身，途之畏者莫如口，期之遠者莫如年。

translations.literal: I once perused the book of Master Guan; it says: "Of burdens, none is heavier than the body; of paths, none is more to be feared than the mouth; of terms, none is more distant than the year.
translations.idiomatic: I once read the book of Master Guan, which says, "Of all burdens, none is heavier than the body; of all paths, none is more to be feared than the mouth; of all terms, none is more distant than the year.

sentences.zh: 以重任行畏途至遠期，惟君子為能及矣。」

translations.literal: To bear a heavy charge, tread a feared path, and reach a distant term—only the noble man can attain this."
translations.idiomatic: To bear a heavy charge, walk a perilous path, and reach a distant term—only the noble man can achieve this."

sentences.zh: 追而味之，喟然長息。

translations.literal: Pondering these words and savoring them, I sighed long and deep.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on these words and savoring them, I sighed long and deep.

sentences.zh: 若夫嶽立而重，有潛戴而不傾；

translations.literal: Consider how a peak stands upright and massive, bearing hidden weight yet never toppling;
translations.idiomatic: Consider how a peak stands upright and massive, bearing hidden weight yet never toppling;

sentences.zh: 山藏稱固，亦趨負而不停；

translations.literal: or hidden mountains said to be firm, yet hurrying onward under their load without pause;
translations.idiomatic: or hidden mountains famed for their firmness, yet hurrying onward under their load without pause;

sentences.zh: 呂梁獨浚，能行歌而匪惕；

translations.literal: at Liang ford alone the waters run deep, yet one can walk and sing without fear;
translations.idiomatic: at Liang ford alone the waters run deep, yet one can walk and sing without fear;

sentences.zh: 焦原作險，或躋踵而不驚。

translations.literal: the heights of Jiaoyuan are perilous, yet some climb step by step unstartled.
translations.idiomatic: the heights of Jiaoyuan are perilous, yet some climb step by step unstartled.

sentences.zh: 九陔方集，故眇然而迅舉；

translations.literal: When the nine embankments are gathered, one rises swiftly and far into the blue;
translations.idiomatic: When the nine embankments are gathered, one soars swiftly into the distant blue;

sentences.zh: 五紀當定，想窅乎而上征。

translations.literal: when the five chronologies are fixed, one mounts upward into the deep beyond.
translations.idiomatic: when the five chronologies are fixed, one mounts upward into the deep beyond.

sentences.zh: 苟任重也有度，則任之而愈固。

translations.literal: If the burden has measure, then bearing it only makes one firmer.
translations.idiomatic: If the burden has measure, then bearing it only makes one firmer.

sentences.zh: 乘危也有術，蓋乘之而靡恤。

translations.literal: If danger has its art, then meeting it only leaves one untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: If danger has its art, then meeting it only leaves one untroubled.

sentences.zh: 彼期遠而能通，果應之而可必。

translations.literal: One who keeps a distant term yet can pass through—truly, meeting it proves sure.
translations.idiomatic: One who keeps a distant term yet can pass through it will surely meet it in the end.

sentences.zh: 豈神理之獨爾，亦人事其如一。

translations.literal: Is this principle divine alone? Human affairs follow the same law.
translations.idiomatic: Is this principle divine alone? Human affairs follow the same law.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 處天壤之間，勞死生之地，攻之以嗜欲，牽之以名利，粱肉不期而共臻，珠玉無足而俱致，於是乎驕奢仍作，危亡旋至。

translations.literal: Living between heaven and earth, toiling on the ground where life and death meet, assailed by appetites, dragged by fame and profit—fine grain and meat arrive unbidden together, pearls and jade come though one has not a foot to walk—then arrogance and extravagance arise in turn, and peril and ruin follow at once.
translations.idiomatic: Living between heaven and earth, toiling on the ground where life and death meet, assailed by appetite and dragged by fame and profit, fine grain and meat arrive unbidden together, pearls and jade come though one has not a foot to walk—and so arrogance and extravagance arise in turn, and peril and ruin follow at once.

sentences.zh: 然同上智大賢，惟幾惟哲，或出或處，不常其時。

translations.literal: Yet likewise for the supreme wise and the greatest worthies, discerning the subtle and wise in judgment, whether they emerge or withdraw, they do not keep to one season.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for the supreme wise and the greatest worthies, discerning the subtle and wise in judgment, whether they emerge or withdraw, they do not keep to one season.

sentences.zh: 其舒也濟世成務，其卷也聲銷跡滅。

translations.literal: In their expansion they aid the age and fulfill its tasks; in their withdrawal voice vanishes and traces disappear.
translations.idiomatic: In their expansion they aid the age and fulfill its tasks; in their withdrawal voice vanishes and traces disappear.

sentences.zh: 玉帛子女，椒蘭律呂，諂諛無所先；

translations.literal: Silks and jade, sons and daughters, spice orchids and pitch pipes—flattery leads to nothing before them;
translations.idiomatic: Silks and jade, sons and daughters, spice orchids and pitch pipes—flattery never leads the way before them;

sentences.zh: 稱肉度骨，膏辱挑舌，怨惡莫之前。

translations.literal: Weighing flesh to measure bone, greasing shame and wagging the tongue—hatred and malice never go before them.
translations.idiomatic: Nitpicking slander, humiliating words and wagging tongues—hatred and malice never go before them.

sentences.zh: 勳名共山河同久，志業與金石比堅。

translations.literal: Meritorious fame endures as long as mountains and rivers; resolve and achievement are hard as metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious fame endures as long as mountains and rivers; resolve and achievement are hard as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋厚棟不橈，遊刃砉然。

translations.literal: This is like a great beam that does not warp, or a blade that slices with a clean sound.
translations.idiomatic: This is like a great beam that does not warp, or a blade that slices with a clean sound.

sentences.zh: 逮于厥德不常，喪其金璞，馳騖人世，鼓動流俗，挾湯日而謂寒，包溪壑而未足。

translations.literal: When one's virtue is not constant, one loses one's golden uncut jade; racing through the human world, stirring vulgar currents, clutching a scorching sun yet calling it cold, hoarding ravines and gorges yet never finding enough.
translations.idiomatic: When one's virtue is not constant, one loses one's golden core; racing through the human world and stirring vulgar currents, one clutches a scorching sun yet calls it cold, hoards ravines and gorges yet never finds enough.

sentences.zh: 源不清而流濁，表不端而影曲。

translations.literal: If the source is not clear the stream runs muddy; if the stem is not straight the shadow bends.
translations.idiomatic: If the source is not clear the stream runs muddy; if the stem is not straight the shadow bends.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 膠漆詎堅，寒暑甚促，反利而成害，化榮而就辱，欣戚更來，得喪仍續。

translations.literal: Can glue and lacquer claim to be firm? Cold and heat pass swiftly. Gain turns to harm, glory to disgrace; joy and sorrow alternate, gain and loss follow unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Can glue and lacquer claim to be firm? Cold and heat pass swiftly. Gain turns to harm, glory to disgrace; joy and sorrow alternate, and gain and loss follow unbroken.

sentences.zh: 至有身禦魑魅，魂沉狴獄。

translations.literal: Some come to bodies assailed by demons, souls sunk in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Some come to bodies assailed by demons and souls sunk in prison.

sentences.zh: 詎非足力不強，迷在當局！

translations.literal: Is it that their strength was insufficient? The delusion lay in being caught in the moment!
translations.idiomatic: Was their strength insufficient? The delusion lay in being caught in the moment!

sentences.zh: 孰可謂車戒前傾，人師先覺？

translations.literal: Who can say that the cart warns of leaning forward, yet men take their teacher to have foreseen all?
translations.idiomatic: Who can say the cart warns of leaning forward, yet men believe their teacher saw it all beforehand?

sentences.zh: 聞諸君子，雅道之士，遊遨經術，厭飫文史。

translations.literal: I have heard, gentlemen, that men of refined principle roam through the classics, sated with letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard, gentlemen, that men of refined principle roam through the classics, sated with letters and history.

sentences.zh: 筆有奇鋒，談有勝理。

translations.literal: Their brushes hold keen edge; their talk holds winning reason.
translations.idiomatic: Their brushes hold keen edge; their talk holds winning reason.

sentences.zh: 孝悌之至，神明通矣。

translations.literal: When filial piety and brotherly respect reach their utmost, the spirits are moved.
translations.idiomatic: When filial piety and brotherly respect reach their utmost, the spirits are moved.

sentences.zh: 審蹈而行，量路而止。

translations.literal: Tread carefully and walk; measure the road and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Tread carefully and walk; measure the road and stop.

sentences.zh: 自我及物，先人後已。

translations.literal: From oneself extend to things; put others first and oneself after.
translations.idiomatic: From oneself extend to things; put others first and oneself after.

sentences.zh: 情無系于榮悴，心靡滯於慍喜。

translations.literal: Feeling is not bound to glory or decline; the heart does not stall on anger or joy.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling is not bound to glory or decline; the heart does not stall on anger or joy.

sentences.zh: 不養望於丘壑，不待價於城市。

translations.literal: Do not cultivate reputation in mountain streams; do not wait for a price in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Do not cultivate reputation in mountain streams; do not wait for a price in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 言行相顧，慎終猶始。

translations.literal: Word and deed look to each other; be careful at the end as at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Word and deed look to each other; be careful at the end as at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 有一于斯，鬱為羽儀。

translations.literal: Have one of these, and you may rise to be an exemplar of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Have one of these, and you may rise to be an exemplar of grace.

sentences.zh: 恪居展事，知無不為，或左或右，則髦士攸宜，無悔無吝，故高而不危。

translations.literal: Dwell reverently and extend your duties; where you know something can be done, do it, whether left or right—then the eminent man is fit for the task; without regret or shame, thus high yet not endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Dwell reverently and extend your duties; where you know something can be done, do it, whether left or right—then the eminent man is fit for the task. Without regret or shame, one stands high yet not endangered.

sentences.zh: 異乎勇進忘退，苟得患失；

translations.literal: Unlike those who press forward bravely and forget retreat, grasping gain and fearing loss;
translations.idiomatic: Unlike those who press forward bravely and forget retreat, grasping gain and fearing loss;

sentences.zh: 射千金之產，徼萬鐘之秩；

translations.literal: staking a fortune of a thousand gold to chase a salary of ten thousand bushels;
translations.idiomatic: staking a fortune of a thousand gold to chase a salary of ten thousand bushels;

sentences.zh: 投烈風之門，趣炎火之室。

translations.literal: casting oneself into gates of fierce wind, rushing toward chambers of blazing fire.
translations.idiomatic: casting oneself into gates of fierce wind, rushing toward chambers of blazing fire.

sentences.zh: 載蹶而墜其貽宴，或蹲乃喪其貞吉。

translations.literal: Tripping and falling from the feast one's ancestors bequeathed, or crouching and losing the firm good fortune [of the hexagram].
translations.idiomatic: Tripping and falling from the feast one's ancestors bequeathed, or crouching and losing the firm good fortune promised by the hexagram.

sentences.zh: 可不畏歟！

translations.literal: Can one not stand in awe!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not stand in awe!

sentences.zh: 可不戒歟！

translations.literal: Can one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not take warning!

sentences.zh: 門有倚禍，事不可不密；

translations.literal: At the door misfortune may lean—affairs must not lack secrecy;
translations.idiomatic: At the door misfortune may lean—affairs must not lack secrecy;

sentences.zh: 牆有伏寇，言不可而失。

translations.literal: In the wall lurk hidden foes—words must not slip.
translations.idiomatic: In the wall lurk hidden foes—words must not slip.

sentences.zh: 宜諦其言，宜端其行。

translations.literal: Consider your words carefully; keep your conduct upright.
translations.idiomatic: Consider your words carefully; keep your conduct upright.

sentences.zh: 言之不善，行之不正，鬼執強梁，人囚徑廷，幽奪其魄，明夭其命。

translations.literal: Speak what is not good, act what is not upright—ghosts seize the violent, men hold you in the open court; in darkness your soul is taken, in daylight your life is cut short.
translations.idiomatic: Speak what is not good, act what is not upright—ghosts seize the violent, men bind you in the open court; in darkness your soul is taken, in daylight your life is cut short.

sentences.zh: 不服非法，不行非道。

translations.literal: Do not submit to what is not lawful; do not walk what is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Do not submit to what is not lawful; do not walk what is not the Way.

sentences.zh: 公鼎為己信，私玉非身寶。

translations.literal: The public cauldron is one's trust; private jade is not the body's treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The public cauldron is one's trust; private jade is not the body's treasure.

sentences.zh: 過涅為紺，逾藍作青，持繩親直，置水觀平。

translations.literal: Pass through indigo and become dark blue; cross beyond blue and become green; hold the plumb line to see straight; set water to observe level.
translations.idiomatic: Pass through indigo and become dark blue; cross beyond blue and become green; hold the plumb line to see straight; set water to observe level.

sentences.zh: 時然後取，未若無欲，知止知足，庶免於辱。

translations.literal: Take only when the time is right—better still to have no desire; know when to stop and know when you have enough, and you may escape disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Take only when the time is right—better still to have no desire; know when to stop and know when you have enough, and you may escape disgrace.

sentences.zh: 是以為必察其幾，舉必慎於微。

translations.literal: Therefore in acting one must scrutinize the subtle signs; in every undertaking one must be careful at the small.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in acting one must scrutinize the subtle signs; in every undertaking one must be careful at the small.

sentences.zh: 知幾慮微，斯亡則稀；

translations.literal: Know the subtle and consider the minute, and ruin will be rare;
translations.idiomatic: Know the subtle and consider the minute, and ruin will be rare;

sentences.zh: 既察且慎，福祿攸歸。

translations.literal: Having scrutinized and been careful, fortune and rank will come to you.
translations.idiomatic: Having scrutinized and been careful, fortune and rank will come to you.

sentences.zh: 昔蘧瑗識四十九非，顏子鄰幾三月不違。

translations.literal: Long ago Qu Boyu looked back on the forty-nine faults he had corrected; Yan Hui was nearly there—for three months he did not stray.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Qu Boyu looked back on the forty-nine faults he had corrected; Yan Hui was nearly there—for three months he did not stray.

sentences.zh: 跬步無已，至於千里；

translations.literal: Half-steps without cease reach a thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: Half-steps without cease reach a thousand li;

sentences.zh: 覆蕢而進，及于萬仞。

translations.literal: Heaping basket upon basket, one advances to ten thousand ren.
translations.idiomatic: Heaping basket upon basket, one advances to ten thousand ren.

sentences.zh: 故云行遠自邇，登高自卑，可大可久，與世推移。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: to go far, start from what is near; to climb high, start from what is low. Great yet lasting, one shifts with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: to go far, start from what is near; to climb high, start from what is low. Great yet lasting, one shifts with the age.

sentences.zh: 月滿如規，後夜則虧；

translations.literal: When the moon is full as a round, after night it wanes;
translations.idiomatic: When the moon is full as a round, after night it wanes;

sentences.zh: 槿榮於枝，望暮而萎。

translations.literal: Hibiscus blooms on the branch, and at evening sight it withers.
translations.idiomatic: Hibiscus blooms on the branch, and at evening sight it withers.

sentences.zh: 夫奚益而不損？

translations.literal: What increases yet does not diminish?
translations.idiomatic: What increases yet does not diminish?

sentences.zh: 孰有損而不害？

translations.literal: What diminishes yet does not harm?
translations.idiomatic: What diminishes yet does not harm?

sentences.zh: 益不欲多，利不欲大。

translations.literal: Increase is not to be desired in excess; profit is not to be desired in magnitude.
translations.idiomatic: Increase is not to be desired in excess; profit is not to be desired in magnitude.

sentences.zh: 唯居德者畏其甚，體真者懼其大。

translations.literal: Only one who dwells in virtue fears its excess; only one who embodies truth dreads its greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Only one who dwells in virtue fears its excess; only one who embodies truth dreads its greatness.

sentences.zh: 道尊則群謗集，任重而眾怨會。

translations.literal: When the Way is honored, slander gathers; when the burden is heavy, resentment converges.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way is honored, slander gathers; when the burden is heavy, resentment converges.

sentences.zh: 其達也則尼父棲遑，其忠也而周公狼狽。

translations.literal: In attaining office Confucius was unsettled; in fulfilling loyalty the Duke of Zhou was harried.
translations.idiomatic: In attaining office Confucius was unsettled; in fulfilling loyalty the Duke of Zhou was harried.

sentences.zh: 無曰人之我狹，在我不可而覆；

translations.literal: Do not say men are narrow toward me—in myself I must not overturn what should not be overturned;
translations.idiomatic: Do not say men are narrow toward me—in myself I must not overturn what should not be overturned;

sentences.zh: 無曰人之我厚，在我不可而咎。

translations.literal: Do not say men are generous toward me—in myself I must not blame when blame is not due.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say men are generous toward me—in myself I must not blame when blame is not due.

sentences.zh: 如山之大，無不有也；

translations.literal: Great as a mountain—there is nothing it does not contain;
translations.idiomatic: Great as a mountain—there is nothing it does not contain;

sentences.zh: 如穀之虛，無不受也。

translations.literal: Empty as a valley—there is nothing it does not receive.
translations.idiomatic: Empty as a valley—there is nothing it does not receive.

sentences.zh: 能剛能柔，重可負也；

translations.literal: Able to be firm and able to be soft, a heavy load can be borne;
translations.idiomatic: Able to be firm and able to be soft, a heavy load can be borne;

sentences.zh: 能信能順，險可走也；

translations.literal: Able to be faithful and able to be yielding, peril can be passed;
translations.idiomatic: Able to be faithful and able to be yielding, peril can be passed;

sentences.zh: 能智能愚，期可久也。

translations.literal: Able to be wise and able to be dull—then endurance may be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Able to be wise and able to be dull—then endurance may be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 周廟之人，三緘其口，漏邑在前，欹器留後，俾諸來裔，傳之坐右。

translations.literal: The man in the Zhou temple thrice sealed his mouth; the leaking cup set before him, the tipping vessel left behind—entrust this to posterity, transmit it to the right hand.
translations.idiomatic: The man in the Zhou temple thrice sealed his mouth; with the leaking cup set before him and the tipping vessel left behind, entrust this to posterity and keep it at your right hand.

sentences.zh: 其後群臣多言魏史不實，武成復敕更審。

translations.literal: Afterward many ministers said the Wei History was not factual; Wucheng again ordered a further review.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward many ministers said the Wei History was not factual, and Emperor Wucheng again ordered a further review.

sentences.zh: 收又回換，遂為盧同立傳，崔綽反更附出。

translations.literal: Shou again reversed exchanges—thus he created a separate biography for Lu Tong, while Cui Chuo was instead attached elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou again reversed his changes, creating a separate biography for Lu Tong while Cui Chuo was instead attached elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 楊愔家傳本云「有魏以來，一門而已」，至是改此八字。

translations.literal: Yang Yin's family biography originally read "since Wei began, one clan alone"—at this point those eight characters were changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin's family biography had originally read "since Wei began, one clan alone"—at this point those eight characters were changed.

sentences.zh: 又先云「弘農華陰人」，乃改「自雲弘農」以配王慧龍「自雲太原人」，此其失也。

translations.literal: It had also first said "a man of Hongnong Huayin," then changed to "himself claimed Hongnong" to match Wang Huilong's "himself claimed Taiyuan"—this was his error.
translations.idiomatic: It had also first said "a man of Hongnong Huayin," then changed to "himself claimed Hongnong" to match Wang Huilong's "himself claimed Taiyuan"—this was his error.

sentences.zh: 尋除開府、中書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Prefecture establishment and Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand Prefecture establishment and Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武成崩，未發喪，在內諸公以後主即位有年，疑於赦令。

translations.literal: When Wucheng died, before the mourning was announced, the lords within the palace, because the Late Ruler had reigned for years, were uncertain about an amnesty decree.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng died, before the mourning was announced, the lords within the palace, because the Late Ruler had already reigned for years, were uncertain about issuing an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸公引收訪焉。

translations.literal: The lords brought Shou in to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: The lords brought Wei Shou in to consult him.

sentences.zh: 收固執宜有恩澤，乃從之。

translations.literal: Shou firmly maintained that grace should be shown, and they followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou firmly maintained that grace should be shown, and they followed him.

sentences.zh: 掌詔誥，除尚書右僕射，總議監一禮事，位特進。

translations.literal: He directed imperial edicts and pronouncements, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, oversaw deliberation and supervision of ritual affairs, and ranked as Special Promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He directed imperial edicts and pronouncements, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, oversaw deliberation and supervision of ritual affairs, and held the rank of Special Promotion.

sentences.zh: 收奏請趙彥深、和士開、徐之才共監，先以告士開，士開驚，辭以不學。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized requesting Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to supervise jointly; he first told Shikai, who was alarmed and declined on grounds of lacking learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou memorialized requesting Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, and Xu Zhicai to supervise jointly; he first told Shikai, who was alarmed and declined on grounds of lacking learning.

sentences.zh: 收曰：「天下事皆由王，五禮非王不決。」

translations.literal: Shou said: "All affairs under heaven are decided by Your Highness; the five rites cannot be settled without Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou said, "All affairs under heaven are decided by Your Highness; the five rites cannot be settled without Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 士開謝而許之。

translations.literal: Shikai apologized and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai apologized and agreed.

sentences.zh: 多引文士令執筆，儒者馬敬德、熊安生、權會實主之。

translations.literal: He invited many literati to hold the brush; the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui were the ones who actually directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: He invited many literati to hold the brush, but the Confucian scholars Ma Jingde, Xiong Ansheng, and Quan Hui were the ones who actually directed the work.

sentences.zh: 武平三年薨，贈司空、尚書左僕射，諡文貞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 有集七十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works totaled seventy fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in seventy fascicles.

sentences.zh: 收碩學大才，然性褊，不能達命體道。

translations.literal: Shou was a great scholar and great talent, yet his nature was narrow, and he could not comprehend fate and embody the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was a learned man of great talent, yet by nature he was narrow-minded and could not grasp fate or embody the Way.

sentences.zh: 見當塗貴遊，每以言色相悅。

translations.literal: When he saw those in power and noble travelers, he always pleased them with his words and expressions.
translations.idiomatic: When he met those in power and the wealthy elite, he always sought to please them with his words and manner.

sentences.zh: 然提獎後輩，以名行為先，浮華輕險之徒，雖有才能，弗重也。

translations.literal: Yet he promoted and encouraged juniors, putting reputation and conduct first; frivolous and reckless types, though talented, he did not esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he encouraged younger men and valued reputation and conduct above all; frivolous and reckless men, however talented, he did not respect.

sentences.zh: 初，河間邢子才、子明及季景與收，並以文章業，世稱大邢小魏，言尤俊也。

translations.literal: At first, Xing Zicai and Ziming of Hejian and Jijing, together with Shou, all made their mark in literature; the age called them Great Xing and Little Wei, saying they were especially brilliant in writing.
translations.idiomatic: In their early days, Xing Zicai and Ziming of Hejian, Jijing, and Wei Shou all made their careers in literature; contemporaries called them Great Xing and Little Wei, for their prose was especially brilliant.

sentences.zh: 收少子才十歲，子才每曰：「佛助，僚人之偉。」

translations.literal: Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai would often say: "Fozhu — a towering figure among peers."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was ten years younger than Zicai; Zicai often said, "Fozhu is a towering figure among his peers."

sentences.zh: 後收稍與子才爭名，文宣貶子才曰：「爾才不及魏收。」

translations.literal: Later Shou gradually competed with Zicai for fame; Emperor Wenxuan belittled Zicai, saying: "Your talent does not match Wei Shou's."
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Shou gradually vied with Zicai for literary fame, and Emperor Wenxuan belittled Zicai, saying, "Your talent does not match Wei Shou's."

sentences.zh: 收益得志，自序云：「先稱溫、邢，後曰邢、魏。」

translations.literal: Shou grew all the more triumphant; in his own preface he wrote: "At first they spoke of Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou became all the more triumphant and wrote in his own preface, "At first they spoke of Wen and Xing; later they said Xing and Wei."

sentences.zh: 然收內陋邢，心不許也。

translations.literal: Yet Shou inwardly looked down on Xing and did not truly accept it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his heart Wei Shou looked down on Xing and never truly accepted it.

sentences.zh: 收既輕疾，好聲樂，善胡舞。

translations.literal: Shou was both frivolous and quick-tempered; he loved music and was skilled at barbarian dances.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was both frivolous and quick-tempered; he loved music and was skilled at foreign dances.

sentences.zh: 文宣末，數於東山與諸優為獼猴與狗鬥，帝寵狎之。

translations.literal: Near the end of Wenxuan's reign, he often performed monkey-versus-dog fights with entertainers on Mount Dong; the emperor favored and treated him familiarly.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Wenxuan's reign, he often staged monkey-versus-dog fights with entertainers on Mount Dong, and the emperor favored and treated him familiarly.

sentences.zh: 收外兄博陵崔岩嘗以雙聲嘲收曰：「遇魏收衰日愚魏。」

translations.literal: Shou's maternal cousin Cui Yan of Boling once mocked Shou with double alliteration, saying: "Meeting Wei Shou on a day of decline — absurd Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Shou's maternal cousin Cui Yan of Boling once mocked him with a double-alliteration pun: "Meeting Wei Shou on a day of decline — absurd Wei."

sentences.zh: 魏答曰：「顏岩腥瘦，是誰所生，羊頤狗頰，頭團鼻平，飯房答籠，著孔嘲玎。」

translations.literal: Wei replied: "Yan the face, rank and lean — whose offspring? Goat chin, dog cheek, round head, flat nose — rice bin, bamboo cage, dressed in holes mocking a ding."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou replied with a retort in kind: "Yan the face, rank and lean — whose offspring? A goat's chin, a dog's cheeks, a round head and flat nose — rice bin, bamboo cage, dressed in tatters to mock a ding."

sentences.zh: 其辯捷不拘若是。

translations.literal: His wit and quickness were unconstrained in just this way.
translations.idiomatic: His wit was quick and unrestrained in just this fashion.

sentences.zh: 既緣史筆，多憾于人，齊亡之歲，收塚被髮，棄其骨於外。

translations.literal: Since he had wielded the historian's brush, he had many grievances against others; in the year Qi perished, Shou's tomb was dug up, his hair disheveled, and his bones cast outside.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had wielded the historian's brush, he had made many enemies; in the year the Qi dynasty fell, his tomb was desecrated, his hair left unkempt, and his bones cast outside.

sentences.zh: 先養弟子仁表為嗣，位至尚書膳部郎中。

translations.literal: He had earlier adopted his disciple Renbiao as heir; Renbiao rose to Gentleman of the Catering Section in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier adopted his disciple Renbiao as his heir; Renbiao rose to Gentleman of the Catering Section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于溫縣令。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he died while serving as magistrate of Wen county.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he died while serving as magistrate of Wen county.

sentences.zh: 子建族子惇，字仲讓。

translations.literal: Dun, a clansman of Zijian, courtesy name Zhongrang.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, a clansman of Zijian, whose courtesy name was Zhongrang.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，性通率。

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing and grand; his nature was straightforward and open.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in appearance and straightforward by nature.

sentences.zh: 永安末，除安東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yong'an era, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 爾硃仲遠鎮東郡，以事捕惇，遇出外，執惇兄子胤而去。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan garrisoned Dong commandery; on account of an affair he sought to arrest Dun, but encountering him away from home, seized Dun's elder brother's son Yin and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhongyuan was stationed in Dong commandery, he sought to arrest Dun over a certain matter; finding Dun away from home, he seized Dun's nephew Yin instead and took him away.

sentences.zh: 惇聞哭曰：「若害胤寧無吾也。」

translations.literal: Dun, hearing, wept and said: "If Yin is harmed, better that I do not exist."
translations.idiomatic: When Dun heard this, he wept and said, "If Yin is harmed, better that I not exist at all."

sentences.zh: 乃見仲遠，叩頭曰：「家事在惇，胤何知也？

translations.literal: Then he went to see Zhongyuan, kowtowed, and said: "Household affairs rest with Dun — what could Yin know of them?
translations.idiomatic: He then went to see Zhongyuan, kowtowed, and said, "Household affairs are my responsibility — what could Yin know of them?

sentences.zh: 乞以身罪。」

translations.literal: I beg to bear the guilt in my own person."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to bear the guilt myself."

sentences.zh: 仲遠義而舍之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan, moved by righteousness, released him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan, moved by his righteousness, released him.

sentences.zh: 天平中，拜衛將軍，右光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he was appointed General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era, he was appointed General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and then died.

sentences.zh: 惇叔偃，字盤蚪。

translations.literal: Dun's uncle Yan, courtesy name Panqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's uncle Yan, whose courtesy name was Panqiu.

sentences.zh: 有當世幹用，位驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He had practical ability for his age and held the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He had practical ability suited to his times and held the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 性浮動，晚乃曲附高肇。

translations.literal: His nature was restless and unstable; only late in life did he abjectly attach himself to Gao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Restless and unstable by nature, he abjectly attached himself to Gao Zhao only late in life.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰之死也，偃構成其事，為時所惡。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie died, Yan fabricated the affair, and was hated by the age.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xie of Pengcheng was killed, Yan fabricated the case against him and was widely despised.

sentences.zh: 子質，字懷素。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, courtesy name Huaisu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, whose courtesy name was Huaisu.

sentences.zh: 幼有立志，年十四，啟母求就徐遵明受業，母以其年幼，不許。

translations.literal: From youth he had set purpose; at fourteen he petitioned his mother to study under Xu Zunming; his mother, considering him too young, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was resolved in purpose; at fourteen he asked his mother to let him study under Xu Zunming, but she refused, thinking him too young.

sentences.zh: 質遂密將一奴，遠赴徐學，留書一紙，置所臥床。

translations.literal: Zhi then secretly took one servant and went far to study with Xu, leaving a note on his sleeping bed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then secretly took a servant and traveled far to study with Xu, leaving a note on his bed.

sentences.zh: 內外見之，相視悲歎。

translations.literal: Those inside and outside saw it and looked at one another with sorrowful sighs.
translations.idiomatic: When the household found it, they looked at one another and sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 五六年中，便通諸經大義。

translations.literal: Within five or six years he had mastered the great meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years he had mastered the essential meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 自學言歸，生徒輻湊，皆同衣食，情若兄弟。

translations.literal: When he said he would return from his studies, students gathered in throngs; all shared food and clothing, affection like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When he announced his return from study, students flocked to him; they shared food and clothing and treated one another like brothers.

sentences.zh: 後避葛榮難，客居趙國飛龍山，為亂賊所害。

translations.literal: Later, fleeing the troubles of Ge Rong, he lived as a guest on Feilong Mountain in Zhao; he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Later, fleeing the chaos of Ge Rong, he lived as a guest on Feilong Mountain in Zhao state and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 士友傷惜之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and friends mourned and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and friends mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，侍中李俊、秘書監常景等三十二人申辭于尚書，為請贈諡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe, Chief Minister Li Jun, Director of the Secretariat Chang Jing, and thirty-two others presented a petition to the Ministry of Works requesting a posthumous title for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe, Chief Minister Li Jun, Director of the Secretariat Chang Jing, and thirty-two others petitioned the Ministry of Works to request a posthumous title for him.

sentences.zh: 事下太常，博士考行，諡曰貞烈先生。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Minister of Ceremonies; the academicians examined his conduct, and his posthumous title was given as Master Zhenlie (Upright and Steadfast).
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Minister of Ceremonies; the academicians examined his conduct and granted the posthumous title Master Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 魏長賢，收之族叔也。

translations.literal: Wei Changxian was Shou's clansman uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Changxian was Wei Shou's uncle by clan relation.

sentences.zh: 祖釗，本名顯義，字弘理，魏世祖賜名，仍命以顯義為字。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao, original name Xianyi, courtesy name Hongli; Emperor Shizu of Wei bestowed the name Zhao and further ordered that Xianyi serve as his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao, whose original name was Xianyi and courtesy name Hongli, was given the name Zhao by Emperor Shizu of Wei, who also designated Xianyi as his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 雅性俊辯，博涉群書，有當世才，兼資文武，知名梁、楚、淮、泗之間。

translations.literal: By nature elegant, brilliant, and eloquent, he broadly traversed all books, had talent for his age, combined civil and military gifts, and was renowned between Liang, Chu, Huai, and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Elegant, brilliant, and eloquent by nature, he read widely and possessed both civil and military talent; he was renowned throughout the regions of Liang, Chu, the Huai, and the Si.

sentences.zh: 世祖南伐，聞而召之，既至，與語大悅。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched south, hearing of him he summoned him; once he arrived and they conversed, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu marched south, he heard of Zhao and summoned him; once Zhao arrived and they spoke, the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 謂釗曰：「今我此行，是卿建功之日，勉之，勿憂不富貴也。」

translations.literal: He said to Zhao: "On this campaign of mine, this is the day for you to achieve merit — exert yourself; do not worry that you will not be rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: He said to Zhao, "On this campaign, this is your day to win distinction — exert yourself, and do not worry that wealth and honor will not follow."

sentences.zh: 授內都直，侍左右。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inner Capital Attendant and served at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inner Capital Attendant and served at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 師次淮南，諸城未有下者。

translations.literal: The army halted at Huainan; none of the cities had yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Huainan, none of the cities had yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 釗乃進曰：「陛下百萬之軍，風行電掃，攻城掠地，所向無前，雖有智者，莫能為計。

translations.literal: Zhao then advanced and said: "Your Majesty's army of a million men sweeps like wind and lightning; besieging cities and seizing territory, wherever it goes none can stand before it — though there were wise men, none could devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty's army of a million men sweeps like wind and lightning; besieging cities and seizing land, it advances wherever it goes — even the wisest men could devise no counterplan.

sentences.zh: 然而師次淮南，已經累日，義陽諸城，猶敢拒守，此非不懼亡滅，自謂必可保全也。

translations.literal: Yet the army has halted at Huainan for many days already, and the cities of Yiyang still dare to resist and hold out — this is not because they do not fear destruction, but because they believe they can surely preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the army has halted at Huainan for many days, and the cities of Yiyang still dare to resist — not because they do not fear destruction, but because they believe they can still save themselves.

sentences.zh: 但陛下卒徒果銳，殺掠尚多，人皆畏威，未甚懷惠，恐一旦降下，妻子不全，所以遲疑，未肯先發。

translations.literal: Only, Your Majesty's soldiers and conscripts are indeed fierce and sharp, and killing and plundering have been considerable; all fear might but have not greatly felt kindness — they fear that once they surrender, wives and children will not be kept whole; therefore they hesitate and are unwilling to take the first step.
translations.idiomatic: But Your Majesty's troops are fierce, and there has been much killing and plunder; the people fear your might but have not yet felt your mercy. They fear that if they surrender, their wives and children will not be spared — and so they hesitate and will not be the first to submit.

sentences.zh: 臣請間入城內，見其豪右，宣達聖心，示以誠信，必當大小相率，面縛請罪。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to enter the city secretly, see its leading families, proclaim Your Majesty's mind, and show sincerity and trust — then surely high and low will follow one another, binding themselves face-forward to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to enter the city secretly, meet its leading families, proclaim Your Majesty's intentions, and show good faith — then surely great and small alike will follow one another and come bound to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 陛下拔其英楚，因而任之，此外諸城，可不勞兵而自定。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty may select their outstanding men and appoint them accordingly; as for the other cities beyond this, they can be settled without laboring the army."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may select their best men and appoint them, and the other cities will submit without need of arms."

sentences.zh: 世祖大喜曰：「所以召卿，本為是耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "The reason I summoned you was precisely for this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "The reason I summoned you was precisely for this.

sentences.zh: 卿今所言，副吾所望。」

translations.literal: What you now say matches what I hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: What you say now matches exactly what I hoped for."

sentences.zh: 釗遂夜入城中，示以危亡之期，開以生全之路，城中大小欣悅，明旦開門出降。

translations.literal: Zhao then entered the city by night, showed them the time of peril and destruction, opened to them the path to preservation of life; high and low in the city rejoiced, and at dawn they opened the gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao then entered the city by night, showed them the hour of destruction and the path to survival; the whole city rejoiced, and at dawn they opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自此而南，望塵款附。

translations.literal: From this point southward, at the sight of dust they sincerely submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From that point southward, cities submitted in droves at the mere sight of advancing dust.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂釗曰：「卿之一言，逾于十萬之師。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Zhao: "Your single statement surpasses an army of a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Zhao, "Your single speech is worth more than an army of a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 揚我信義，播於四表，實卿一人之力。」

translations.literal: You have spread my faith and righteousness to the four quarters — truly the power of you alone."
translations.idiomatic: You have spread my good faith to the four quarters — truly this is the work of you alone."

sentences.zh: 即授義陽太守、陵江將軍。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed him Administrator of Yiyang and General Who Crosses the River.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Zhao Administrator of Yiyang and General Who Crosses the River.

sentences.zh: 又令釗與諸將，統兵討襲，所當無不摧破，軍中服其勇敢。

translations.literal: He further ordered Zhao together with the other generals to command troops in punitive raids; wherever they went nothing failed to be shattered; the army respected his bravery.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered Zhao to join the other generals in leading punitive raids; wherever they went nothing withstood them, and the army respected his courage.

sentences.zh: 世祖益喜，謂群臣曰：「中國士人，吾拔擢咸盡，文武膽略，未有若釗儔。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was still more pleased and said to the assembled ministers: "Among the gentlemen of China, I have promoted them all — in civil and military courage and strategy, none compares with Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more pleased and said to his ministers, "Of the Chinese gentlemen I have promoted, none matches Zhao in civil and military courage and strategy."

sentences.zh: 加授建忠將軍，追贈其父處順州刺史。

translations.literal: He additionally appointed him General Who Establishes Loyalty and posthumously granted his father the post of Governor of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He further appointed Zhao General Who Establishes Loyalty and posthumously granted his father the post of Governor of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 時經略江左，方大用之，遇風疾發動，頻降醫藥，竟不痊復。

translations.literal: At the time he was planning to seize the Jiangzuo region and was just about to employ Zhao on a great scale, when Zhao suffered a relapse of wind ailment; medicine was repeatedly sent down, yet he never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was planning to seize the lower Yangtze and was about to employ Zhao on a great scale, when he suffered a relapse of paralysis; the emperor repeatedly sent physicians and medicine, but he never recovered.

sentences.zh: 卒時年六十四。

translations.literal: When he died he was sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 父彥，字惠卿，博學善屬文。

translations.literal: His father Yan, courtesy name Huiqing, was learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan, whose courtesy name was Huiqing, was learned and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王幹避開府參軍，廣陵王羽辟記室，並不行。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan offered him Opening Staff Attendant; Prince of Guangling Yu invited him as Record Keeper — he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gan of Zhao commandery offered him a post on his staff and Prince Yu of Guangling invited him as record keeper, he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 陳留公李崇甚重之，引為鎮西參軍事。

translations.literal: Duke of Chenliu Li Chong greatly valued him and brought him in as Western Garrison Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Duke of Chenliu, valued him highly and brought him in as staff officer of the Western Garrison.

sentences.zh: 崇討叛氏陽珍、叛蠻魯北燕，又請為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Chong campaigned against the rebellious Di Yang Zhen and the rebellious tribesman Lu Beiyan, he again requested Yan as Record Keeper Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong campaigned against the rebellious Di chieftain Yang Zhen and the tribal rebel Lu Beiyan, he again asked Yan to serve as record keeper on his staff.

sentences.zh: 中山王英討淮南，又請為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned against Huainan, he again requested Yan as Record Keeper Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan campaigned against Huainan, he again asked Yan to serve as record keeper on his staff.

sentences.zh: 軍還，求為著作郎，思樹不朽之業。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he requested to be a Compiler in the History Office, intending to establish an imperishable enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he requested appointment as Compiler in the History Office, hoping to establish a work that would outlast him.

sentences.zh: 以晉書作者多家，體制繁雜，欲正其紕繆，刪其遊辭，勒成一家之典。

translations.literal: Because there were many authors of the History of Jin and the form was complex and disorderly, he wished to correct its errors, delete its superfluous rhetoric, and compile it into a single authoritative work.
translations.idiomatic: Because many men had written versions of the History of Jin and the form was complex and disorderly, he wished to correct its errors, cut its superfluous rhetoric, and compile a definitive edition.

sentences.zh: 俄而彭城王聞李崇稱之，復請為掾，兼知主客郎中，書遂不成。

translations.literal: Soon Prince of Pengcheng, hearing Li Chong praise him, again requested him as staff officer, additionally overseeing the Master of Guests Attendant; the book was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Pengcheng, hearing Li Chong praise him, again invited him onto his staff and additionally made him Master of Guests Attendant — and the book was never finished.

sentences.zh: 王遇害，退歸田里。

translations.literal: When the prince met with calamity, he withdrew and returned to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was killed, he withdrew to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 清河王復引為諮議。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe again brought him in as Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qinghe again brought him in as adviser.

sentences.zh: 王勢高名重，深為權幸所疾，恐罹其禍，固辭以疾。

translations.literal: The prince's power was high and his fame weighty; he was deeply hated by those in power and favored; fearing to suffer calamity, Yan firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was powerful and eminent, and deeply hated by the powerful and favored at court; fearing to be caught up in the disaster, Yan firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，拜驃騎長史，尋轉光州刺史。
