translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Flying Cavalry General; soon he was transferred to Governor of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, he was appointed chief administrator to the General of Flying Cavalry; soon after he was transferred to Governor of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 年六十八，卒。

translations.literal: At sixty-eight he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 兄伯胤之歸也，留長賢與弟德振，使宦學於洛中。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Boyin returned, he left Changxian and his younger brother Dezheng behind to study in official service at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Boyin returned home, he left Changxian and his younger brother Dezheng in Luoyang to pursue official studies.

sentences.zh: 孝靜北遷，亦徙居鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaojing moved north, they also relocated to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing moved the capital north, they relocated to Ye as well.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，詞藻清華，舉秀才，除汝南王悅參軍事。

translations.literal: He broadly traversed the classics and histories; his literary style was clear and splendid; he was raised as Presented Scholar and appointed Staff Officer to Prince of Runan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories; his prose was clear and elegant; raised as Presented Scholar, he was appointed staff officer to Prince Yue of Runan.

sentences.zh: 入齊，平陽王淹辟為法曹參軍，轉著作佐郎。

translations.literal: After entering Qi, Prince of Pingyang Yan invited him as Legal Section Staff Officer; he was transferred to Assistant Compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi regime was established, Prince Yan of Pingyang invited him as legal section staff officer, and he was later transferred to Assistant Compiler in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 更撰晉書，欲還成先志。

translations.literal: He again composed the History of Jin, wishing to fulfill his father's earlier purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He took up the History of Jin again, hoping to fulfill his father's earlier ambition.

sentences.zh: 河清中，上書譏刺時政，大忤權幸，為上黨屯留令。

translations.literal: During Heqing, he submitted a memorial satirizing current affairs, greatly offending those in power and favored; he was made Magistrate of Tunliu in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Heqing era, he submitted a memorial satirizing current affairs, greatly offending the powerful and favored at court, and was demoted to Magistrate of Tunliu in Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 親故以長賢不相時而動，或為書以相規責。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends, considering that Changxian acted without fitting the times, sometimes wrote letters to admonish and reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends, thinking Changxian had acted without regard for the times, sometimes wrote to admonish and reprove him.

sentences.zh: 長賢復書曰：

translations.literal: Changxian replied in a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Changxian replied in a letter:

sentences.zh: 日者惠書，義高旨遠。

translations.literal: The other day you graciously sent a letter — its principles lofty and its purport far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The other day you graciously sent a letter — lofty in principle and far-reaching in intent.

sentences.zh: 誨僕以自求諸已，思不出位，國之大事，君與執政所圖。

translations.literal: You instructed me to seek within myself, that thought should not exceed one's position, and that the great affairs of the state are for the ruler and those in power to plan.
translations.idiomatic: You admonished me to look within myself, to keep my thoughts within my station, and to leave the great affairs of state to the ruler and those who govern.

sentences.zh: 又謂僕祿不足以代耕，位不登於執戟，幹非其議，自貽悔咎。

translations.literal: You also said my salary is insufficient to replace farming, my rank does not reach that of Halberd Bearer, my meddling was not my place to discuss, and I have brought regret and blame upon myself.
translations.idiomatic: You also said my salary is insufficient to live on, my rank does not reach that of Halberd Bearer, my interference was outside my proper role, and I have brought remorse upon myself.

sentences.zh: 勤勤懇懇，誠見故人之心。

translations.literal: Earnestly and sincerely — truly this shows the heart of an old friend.
translations.idiomatic: Earnest and sincere — truly this shows the heart of an old friend.

sentences.zh: 靜言再思，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: Quietly speaking, upon further reflection, I shall not forget it waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: On quiet reflection, again and again, I shall not forget it waking or sleeping.

sentences.zh: 僕雖固陋，亦嘗奉教于君子矣。

translations.literal: Though I am obstinate and unlearned, I have also once received instruction from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am stubborn and uncultivated, I have also received instruction from gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以為士之立身，其路不一。

translations.literal: I consider that in how a gentleman establishes himself, the paths are not one.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that in how a gentleman establishes himself, the paths are not all the same.

sentences.zh: 故有負鼎俎以趨世，隱漁釣以待時，操築傅岩之下，取履圯橋之上者矣。

translations.literal: Thus there are those who carried cauldrons and sacrificial stands to hurry into the world, hid in fishing and angling to await the times, wielded building tools beneath Mount Fu, and picked up a shoe above the Broken Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Some rushed into public life bearing cooking vessels and sacrificial stands; others hid in fishing and angling to await their hour; some labored with building tools beneath Mount Fu, and others retrieved a shoe above the Broken Bridge.

sentences.zh: 或有釋賃車以匡霸業，委挽輅以定王基，由斬祛以見禮，因射鉤而受相者矣。

translations.literal: Some cast aside a hired cart to aid hegemony, entrusted a hand-drawn carriage to establish a royal foundation, received courtesy through cutting a sleeve, and received chancellorship through shooting at a hook.
translations.idiomatic: Some cast aside a hired cart to aid a hegemonic enterprise; others entrusted a hand-drawn carriage to establish a royal foundation; some won favor by cutting off a sleeve, and others became chancellor because of an arrow shot at a hook.

sentences.zh: 或有三黜不移，屈身以直道；

translations.literal: Some were thrice dismissed yet unmoved, bowing the body to uphold the straight Way;
translations.idiomatic: Some were dismissed three times yet never swayed, humbling themselves to uphold the straight Way;

sentences.zh: 九死不侮，甘心於苦節者矣。

translations.literal: nine deaths yet no regret, willing in bitter steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: others endured nine deaths without regret, content in bitter steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 皆奮於泥滓，自致青云。

translations.literal: All rose from mud and mire to reach the blue clouds themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All rose from the mud to reach the azure heights themselves.

sentences.zh: 雖事有萬殊，而理終一致，榷其大要，歸乎忠孝而已矣。

translations.literal: Though affairs have ten thousand differences, principle in the end is one; weighing the great essentials, it returns to loyalty and filial piety, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Though circumstances differ in countless ways, the principle is ultimately one: weighed in the largest sense, it comes down to loyalty and filial piety, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 夫孝則竭力所生，忠則致身所事，未有孝而遺其親，忠而後其君者也。

translations.literal: Filial piety means exhausting one's strength for those who gave one life; loyalty means giving one's body to what one serves — never has there been filial piety that abandoned one's parents, or loyalty that put one's lord last.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety means devoting one's full strength to those who gave one life; loyalty means giving one's body to one's lord — there has never been filial piety that abandoned one's parents, or loyalty that put one's lord last.

sentences.zh: 僕自射策金馬，記言麟閣，寒暑迭運，五稔於茲。

translations.literal: I, from answering policy questions at the Golden Horse Gate and recording words in the Unicorn Pavilion, seasons of cold and heat have alternated — five harvest-years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Since I passed the policy examination at the Golden Horse Gate and served as a recorder in the Unicorn Pavilion, five years of seasons have passed.

sentences.zh: 不能勒成一家，潤色鴻業，善述人事，功既闕如，顯親揚名，邈焉無冀。

translations.literal: Unable to complete an independent work, adorn the great enterprise, and well narrate human affairs—my merit is already lacking; to glorify my parents and spread my name is far beyond hope.
translations.idiomatic: I have not been able to finish a work of my own, polish the grand imperial enterprise, or ably recount human affairs—my achievements fall woefully short, and to bring honor to my parents and make a name for myself is a hope I must abandon.

sentences.zh: 每一念之，曷雲其已。

translations.literal: Every time I think of it, how can I say it will stop?
translations.idiomatic: Each time these thoughts arise, how could they ever cease?

sentences.zh: 自頃王室板蕩，彝倫攸斁，大臣持祿而莫諫，小臣畏罪而不言，虛痛朝危，空哀主辱。

translations.literal: Recently the royal house has been in turmoil, moral order decayed; great ministers hold their salaries yet do not remonstrate, minor officials fear punishment and do not speak—vainly grieving the court's peril, vainly mourning the lord's disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the royal house has been shaken to its foundations and moral order has collapsed. Great ministers clung to their stipends but offered no remonstrance; minor officials feared punishment and held their tongues. They grieved in vain over the court's peril and mourned in vain the sovereign's humiliation.

sentences.zh: 匪躬之故，徒聞其語；

translations.literal: For the sake of giving one's body for the ruler, one only hears the words;
translations.idiomatic: People speak of sacrificing oneself for the sovereign, but one hears only the words;

sentences.zh: 有犯無隱，未見其人。

translations.literal: Having offenses without concealment—yet no such person is seen.
translations.idiomatic: They cite the principle of remonstrating without concealment, yet no one who actually does so is to be found.

sentences.zh: 此梅福所以獻書，硃雲所以請劍者也。

translations.literal: This is why Mei Fu submitted his letter and Zhu Yun requested the sword.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely why Mei Fu submitted his memorial and Zhu Yun demanded the sword to execute the minister who deceived the emperor.

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，嫠不恤緯而憂宗周之亡，女不懷歸而悲太子之少，況僕之先人，世傳儒業，訓僕以為子之道，曆僕以事君之節？

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that a widow does not worry about her weaving but grieves the fall of the Zhou house; a woman does not long to return home but laments that the crown prince is young—how much more so, when my forebears passed down Confucian learning through the generations, instructing me in the way of being a son and impressing upon me the integrity of serving a lord?
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard it said that a widow will neglect her weaving to grieve over the fall of the house of Zhou, and a woman will set aside her longing for home to mourn that the crown prince is still young. How much more ought I to act thus, when my ancestors handed down Confucian learning for generations, teaching me the duty of a son and drilling into me the integrity owed to one's lord?

sentences.zh: 今僕之委質，有年世矣，安可自同於匹庶，取笑於兒女子哉！

translations.literal: Now I have pledged my allegiance for many years—how can I align myself with common folk and invite ridicule from women and children!
translations.idiomatic: I have pledged myself to service for many years now. How could I lower myself to the level of common people and become a laughingstock for women and children?

sentences.zh: 是以腸一夕而九回，心終朝而百慮，懼當年之不立，恥沒世而無聞，慷慨懷古，自強不息，庶幾伯夷之風，以立懦夫之志。

translations.literal: Therefore my intestines turn nine times in a single night, my heart harbors a hundred thoughts all morning; I fear failing to establish myself in my prime, and am ashamed to leave the world unknown; ardently cherishing antiquity, unceasing in self-strengthening, I hope in some measure for the spirit of Boyi, to rouse the resolve of cowards.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason my thoughts churn through the night and my mind weighs a hundred anxieties by morning. I fear accomplishing nothing while I still have strength, and I am ashamed to die without leaving any mark upon the world. Inspired by the past and striving without rest, I hope in some small way to emulate the spirit of Boyi and awaken even the faint-hearted to resolve.

sentences.zh: 吾子又謂僕幹進務入，不畏友朋；

translations.literal: You further say that I scramble for advancement and rush in without regard, not fearing my friends;
translations.idiomatic: You also accuse me of scrambling for advancement and thrusting myself forward heedlessly, without respect for my friends;

sentences.zh: 居下訕上，欲益反損。

translations.literal: Dwelling below yet mocking those above—wishing to benefit but actually harming.
translations.idiomatic: of standing below yet mocking those above, intending to do good but achieving the opposite.

sentences.zh: 僕誠不敏，以貽吾子之羞，默默苟容，又非平生之意。

translations.literal: I am truly dull-witted and have brought shame upon you; to remain silent and endure passively is also not my lifelong intent.
translations.idiomatic: I am indeed dull-witted and have brought shame upon you. Yet to remain silent and passively endure is equally contrary to what I have stood for all my life.

sentences.zh: 故願得鋤彼草茅，逐茲鳥雀，去一惡，樹一善，不違先旨，以沒九泉。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish to hoe out that wild grass, drive off these sparrows, remove one evil and plant one good, not violating my ancestors' instruction, so as to die in the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I wish to root out that harmful growth and drive off these destructive birds—to remove one evil and establish one good, not betraying my ancestors' teaching, even unto death.

sentences.zh: 求仁得仁，其誰敢怨？

translations.literal: Seeking benevolence and obtaining benevolence—who would dare complain?
translations.idiomatic: Having sought righteousness and found it, who could have grounds for complaint?

sentences.zh: 但言與不言在我，用與不用在時。

translations.literal: Only whether to speak or not to speak is up to me; whether to employ or not to employ is up to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I speak or stay silent is my own choice; whether my words are heeded depends on the times.

sentences.zh: 若國道方屯，時不我與，以忠獲罪，以信見疑，貝錦成章，青蠅變色，良田敗於邪徑，黃金鑠於眾口，窮達運也，其如命何！

translations.literal: If the nation's way is still in hardship and the times do not favor me, and loyalty brings punishment while integrity invites suspicion—when slander weaves its patterns like brocade and flies darken the truth, when good fields are ruined by crooked paths and gold is melted by many mouths—advancement and obscurity are matters of fortune; what can one do against fate!
translations.idiomatic: If the nation's course remains troubled and the times are not with me—if loyalty earns punishment and sincerity invites suspicion, if calumny weaves its patterns and rumor darkens the truth, if good land is ruined by ill paths and pure gold is corroded by many tongues—then success and failure belong to fortune. What can one do against destiny?

sentences.zh: 吾子忠告之言，敢不敬承嘉惠。

translations.literal: Your words of sincere advice—I dare not fail to respectfully receive this fine favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your sincere counsel—I dare not fail to receive it with gratitude and respect.

sentences.zh: 然則僕之所懷，未可一二為俗人道也。

translations.literal: Thus what I hold in my heart cannot in one or two points be told to ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: What I carry in my heart, however, cannot readily be explained to the common run of people.

sentences.zh: 投筆而已，乂復何言！

translations.literal: I put down my brush—that is all; what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: I lay down my brush and have nothing more to say!

sentences.zh: 是出也，人皆為之怏怏，而長賢處之怡然，不屑懷抱，識者以此多焉。

translations.literal: When he went out on this occasion, everyone was resentful on his behalf, yet Changxian bore it with ease, disdaining to brood over it; the discerning praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: On this dismissal, everyone resented it on his behalf, but Changxian accepted it with equanimity, refusing to dwell on resentment. Those who understood admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 武平中，辭疾去職，終於齊代，不復出仕。

translations.literal: During Wuping, he pleaded illness and left office; he ended his days in the Qi realm and never took office again.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era he resigned on grounds of illness and lived out his days in the Qi region, never holding office again.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，搜揚才俊，辟書屢降，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he sought out talented men; summons came repeatedly, but he steadfastly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi and sought out men of talent, appointment letters arrived again and again, but he consistently declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he was posthumously honored as Governor of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子征。

translations.literal: His son was Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zheng.

sentences.zh: 魏季景，收族叔也。

translations.literal: Wei Jijing was Shou's clansman and elder uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jijing was Wei Shou's clansman and elder uncle.

sentences.zh: 父鸞字雙和，為魏文賜名。

translations.literal: His father Luan, courtesy name Shuanghe, was given this name by Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luan, courtesy name Shuanghe, received that name as a bestowment from Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 有器幹，體貌魁偉，以有容儀，為奉車都尉。

translations.literal: He had capacity and ability, a tall and imposing physique; because of his dignified bearing he was made Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed talent and capability and a tall, imposing physique. Because of his dignified appearance he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 曾升輅車，觸毀金翼，斂容請罪。

translations.literal: Once when mounting the imperial carriage he bumped and damaged the golden wing ornament; he composed his countenance and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Once when boarding the imperial carriage he accidentally damaged the golden wing ornament; he composed himself and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿體貌過人，素不便習，何足懼也？」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Your physique surpasses others'; you are by nature unaccustomed to this—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Your stature exceeds that of most men, and you are naturally unused to such things—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 車駕南征漢陽，除鸞統軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south to conquer Hanyang, Luan was appointed commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south against Hanyang, Luan was appointed army commander.

sentences.zh: 帝曆幸其營，歎賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly visited his camp and praised him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly visited his camp and expressed admiration.

sentences.zh: 及在馬圈不豫，敕兼武衛將軍，領宿衛左右。

translations.literal: When at Maquan he was unwell, he was ordered to serve concurrently as General of the Martial Guard, commanding the palace guards at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill at Maquan, he was ordered to serve concurrently as General of the Martial Guard, commanding the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 景明中，六輔之廢，鸞頗預其事。

translations.literal: During Jingming, in the abolition of the Six Assistants, Luan took considerable part in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era, in the removal of the Six Assistants, Luan played a significant role.

sentences.zh: 後除光州刺史，更滿還朝，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Guangzhou; when his term ended he returned to court and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Guang Prefecture. When his term expired he returned to court and died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰夷。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Yi ("Plain").

sentences.zh: 子季景少孤，清苦自立，博學有文才，弱冠有名京師。

translations.literal: His son Jijing was orphaned young, endured hardship and stood on his own, was broadly learned with literary talent, and was famous in the capital before reaching maturity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jijing lost his father young. He endured hardship and supported himself, was widely learned and possessed literary talent, and was already renowned in the capital before reaching twenty.

sentences.zh: 時邢子明稱有才學，殆與子才相侔，季景與收相亞，洛中號兩邢二魏。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Ziming was praised for talent and learning, nearly equal to Zicai; Jijing was ranked alongside Shou—the capital called them the Two Xings and Two Weis.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xing Ziming was acclaimed for scholarship, nearly equal to Xing Zicai. Jijing was ranked just below Wei Shou. In Luoyang they were known as the Two Xings and the Two Weis.

sentences.zh: 莊帝時，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Zhuang's reign, he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Zhuang he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: During Putai, he was Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era he served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 季景善附會，宰要當朝，必先事其左右。

translations.literal: Jijing was skilled at currying favor; when powerful ministers held court, he would always first attend to their attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jijing was adept at ingratiating himself. When a powerful minister held sway, he would always cultivate that minister's close associates first.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆特賞愛之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong especially prized and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong especially valued and favored him.

sentences.zh: 于時才名甚盛，頗過其實。

translations.literal: At the time his reputation for talent was very great, exceeding the reality considerably.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his reputation for talent ran very high, considerably beyond what he deserved.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，位給事黃門侍郎，甚見信待，除定州大中正。

translations.literal: During Taichang, he held the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was greatly trusted, and was appointed Chief Rectifier of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang era he served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, enjoyed great trust, and was appointed Chief Rectifier of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝釋奠，季景與溫子升、李業興、竇瑗等俱為摘句。

translations.literal: At Emperor Xiaowu's libation ceremony, Jijing together with Wen Zisheng, Li Yexing, Dou Yuan, and others all served as phrase selectors.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xiaowu's libation ceremony for Confucius, Jijing joined Wen Zisheng, Li Yexing, Dou Yuan, and others in selecting passages for recitation.

sentences.zh: 天平初，因遷都，遂居柏人西山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, because of the capital's relocation, he then settled on West Mountain at Bairen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era, following the move of the capital, he settled on West Mountain near Bairen.

sentences.zh: 內懷憂悔，乃為擇居賦。

translations.literal: Harboring inward grief and regret, he then composed the "Rhapsody on Choosing a Dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: Troubled inwardly by grief and regret, he composed the "Rhapsody on Choosing a Dwelling."

sentences.zh: 元象初，兼給事黃門侍郎，後兼散騎常侍，使梁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; later he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and was envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanxiang era he concurrently served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; later he also served as Regular Attendant and was sent as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 還，曆大司農卿、魏郡尹。

translations.literal: On return, he successively served as Minister of Grand Granaries and Prefect of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he successively served as Minister of Grand Granaries and Prefect of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，家無餘財，遺命薄葬，贈散騎常侍、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He died; the family had no surplus wealth; his final instructions called for a simple burial; he was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving no surplus wealth at home. His final instructions called for a simple burial. He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆二百餘篇。

translations.literal: His literary writings numbered more than two hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He authored more than two hundred literary works.

sentences.zh: 子澹知名。

translations.literal: His son Dan was well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dan became well known.

sentences.zh: 澹字彥深。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Yanshen.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, styled Yanshen.

sentences.zh: 年十五而孤，專精好學，高才善屬文。

translations.literal: Orphaned at age fifteen, he devoted himself wholly to learning, possessed great talent and skill in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fifteen, he devoted himself to study with singular dedication. He possessed great talent and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，殿中侍御史，預修五禮，及撰御覽。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was Palace Attendant Censor, participated in compiling the Five Rites, and in drafting the Imperial Overview.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Qi as Palace Attendant Censor, participated in compiling the Five Rites, and helped draft the Imperial Overview.

sentences.zh: 除殿中郎、中書舍人，與李德林修國史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Gentleman and Secretariat Aide, and with Li Delin revised the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Gentleman and Secretariat Aide, and collaborated with Li Delin on revising the national history.

sentences.zh: 入周為納言中士。

translations.literal: Entering Zhou, he became Senior Clerk of the Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou conquered Qi he served as Senior Clerk in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隋初，為行台禮部侍郎，尋為聘陳使主。

translations.literal: In early Sui, he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites of the Executive Board; soon he became chief envoy on a mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Sui he served as Vice Director of Rites on the Executive Board, and soon afterward headed an embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 還，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: On return, he was appointed Attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 廢太子勇深禮之，令注庚信集，撰笑苑，世稱博物。

translations.literal: The deposed Crown Prince Yong treated him with deep respect, had him annotate the collected works of Yu Xin, and compose the "Garden of Laughter"; the world called him broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Crown Prince Yong treated him with great respect, commissioned him to annotate Yu Xin's collected works and to compile the Garden of Laughter, and he was widely acclaimed as a man of encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，仍為太子學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Library and continued as academician to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Library and continued to serve as an academician to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝以魏收所撰後魏書褒貶失實，平繪為中興書事不倫序，詔澹別成魏史。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Wei Shou's History of Later Wei had inaccurate praise and blame, and that Ping Hui's account of the restoration was disorderly in arrangement; he ordered Dan to compile a separate Wei history.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Wei Shou's History of Later Wei distorted praise and blame, and that Ping Hui's account of the restoration was disorderly. He ordered Yanshen to compile a separate history of Wei.

sentences.zh: 澹自道武下及恭帝，為十二紀，七十八列傳。

translations.literal: Dan, from Emperor Daowu down to Emperor Gongdi, made twelve annals and seventy-eight biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen's work, from Emperor Daowu down to Emperor Gongdi, comprised twelve annals and seventy-eight biographies.

sentences.zh: 別為史論及例，各一卷，合九十二卷。

translations.literal: Separately there were historical appraisals and precedents, one scroll each, totaling ninety-two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote separate historical appraisals and precedents, one scroll each, for a total of ninety-two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 義例與魏收多所不同。

translations.literal: The principles and precedents differed considerably from those of Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Its principles and precedents differed considerably from those of Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「臣聞天子者繼天立稱，終始絕。

translations.literal: The first states: "I have heard that the Son of Heaven inherits Heaven to establish his title—from beginning to end this is absolute.
translations.idiomatic: The first principle states: "I have heard that the Son of Heaven inherits the Mandate of Heaven to establish his title—a rule that holds absolutely from first to last.

sentences.zh: 故谷梁傳：'太上不名。

translations.literal: Therefore the Guliang Commentary says: 'The Supreme One is not named.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Guliang Commentary says, 'The Supreme One is not referred to by personal name.'

sentences.zh: '曲禮：'天子不言出，諸侯不生名。

translations.literal: 'The Record of Rites says: 'The Son of Heaven does not speak of going out; feudal lords are not named while living.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, 'The Son of Heaven does not speak of going out; feudal lords are not named by their personal names while still living.'

sentences.zh: '諸侯尚不生名，況天子乎？

translations.literal: If even feudal lords are not named while living, how much more the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: If even feudal lords are not named while alive, how much more so the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 若為太子，必須書名。

translations.literal: If one is the crown prince, the name must be written.
translations.idiomatic: If the subject is the crown prince, his personal name must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 良由子者對父生稱，父前子名，禮之意也。

translations.literal: Truly because a son uses his birth name when facing his father—before the father the son is named; such is the intent of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: This is because a son uses his birth name when addressing his father—to name the son before the father is the proper meaning of ritual.

sentences.zh: 至如馬遷，周之太子，並皆言名，漢之儲兩，俱沒其諱，以尊漢卑周，臣子之意也。

translations.literal: As for Sima Qian, the Zhou crown princes—all are spoken of by name; the Han heirs—all have their taboo names obscured—honoring Han and demeaning Zhou: the intent of a subject and son.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian, for instance, names the Zhou crown princes outright, yet obscures the taboo names of Han heirs—honoring Han while demeaning Zhou, reflecting the bias of a Han subject.

sentences.zh: 竊謂雖立此理，恐非其義。

translations.literal: I privately consider that although this principle is established, I fear it is not correct in principle.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that although this principle has been established, it is likely not sound in substance.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 春秋、禮記，太子必書名，天王不言出，此仲尼之褒貶，皇王之稱謂，非當時與異代，遂為優劣也。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals and Record of Rites, the crown prince must be named and the Heavenly King is not spoken of as going out—this is Confucius's praise and blame, the designations of emperors and kings; it is not that contemporaries versus later ages thereby become superior or inferior.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Record of Rites, crown princes are always named and the Heavenly King is never said to 'go out.' These reflect Confucius's standards of praise and blame and the proper forms of address for sovereigns—they do not mean that contemporary versus later dynasties are inherently superior or inferior.

sentences.zh: 班固、范曄、陳壽、王隱、沈約參差不同，尊卑失序。

translations.literal: Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, Wang Yin, and Shen Yue differ variously—honor and humility fall out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu, Fan Ye, Chen Shou, Wang Yin, and Shen Yue applied inconsistent standards, reversing proper order of respect.

sentences.zh: 至於魏收諱儲君之名，書天子之字，過又甚焉。

translations.literal: As for Wei Shou, he tabooed the heir's name yet wrote the Son of Heaven's style name—the excess was even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou went even further, tabooing the crown prince's name while recording the emperor's style name.

sentences.zh: 今所撰，諱皇帝名，書太子字，欲尊君卑臣，依春秋之義。」

translations.literal: In what is now compiled, we taboo the emperor's name and write the crown prince's style name, wishing to honor the lord and humble the minister, following the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals."
translations.idiomatic: In the present work we taboo the emperor's personal name and record the crown prince's style name, seeking to honor the sovereign and humble the subject in accordance with the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals."

sentences.zh: 二曰「魏氏平文以前，部落之君長耳。

translations.literal: The second states: "Before Emperor Pingwen of Wei, the Wei clan were merely chieftains of a tribal confederation.
translations.idiomatic: The second principle states: "Before Emperor Pingwen, the house of Wei were merely tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 太祖遠追二十八帝，並極崇高，違堯舜憲章，越周公典禮。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor traced back twenty-eight emperors, all elevated to the utmost eminence—contravening the institutions of Yao and Shun and exceeding the canonical rites of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor traced the lineage back twenty-eight generations, elevating all to the highest eminence—in violation of the model of Yao and Shun and beyond the canonical rites established by the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 但道武出自結繩，未師典誥，當須南董直筆，裁而正之；

translations.literal: But Emperor Daowu arose from the age of knotted cords, untutored in the classical edicts—what was needed was the straightforward brush of the Southern and Dong historians to judge and correct this;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu belonged to an age that predated written law and had no training in the classical canon. What was needed was the impartial brush of a true historian to judge and set matters right;

sentences.zh: 反更飾非，豈是觀過？

translations.literal: Instead errors were further embellished—is this observing faults?
translations.idiomatic: Instead errors were glossed over—is this the way to observe and correct faults?

sentences.zh: 但力微天女所誕，靈異絕世，尊為始祖，得禮之宜。

translations.literal: But Emperor Liwei was born of a heavenly maiden, miraculously exceptional in the world—honoring him as Founding Ancestor accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Liwei, however, was born of a heavenly maiden and possessed miraculous gifts beyond the ordinary. Honoring him as Founding Ancestor was ritually appropriate.

sentences.zh: 平文、昭成，雄據塞表，英風漸盛，圖南之業，基自此始。

translations.literal: Emperors Pingwen and Zhaocheng held the borderlands heroically; their heroic wind gradually flourished—the enterprise of turning south had its foundation from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Pingwen and Zhaocheng held the northern frontier with force; their prestige steadily grew, and the ambition to advance south had its foundation in their reigns.

sentences.zh: 長孫斤之亂也，兵交御坐，太子授命，昭成獲免。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Changsun Jin, weapons crossed at the imperial seat; the crown prince received the command and Zhaocheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: During the uprising of Changsun Jin, fighting reached the imperial throne itself. The crown prince took command and Zhaocheng was saved.

sentences.zh: 道武此時，後緡方娠，宗廟復存，社稷有主，大功大孝，實在獻明。

translations.literal: At this time the empress dowager was newly pregnant; the ancestral temple was preserved and the altars of state had their lord—the great merit and great filial piety truly belonged to Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Daowu was not yet born—the empress dowager was newly pregnant with him. The ancestral temple was preserved and the realm had its sovereign. The great achievement and great filial devotion truly belonged to Emperor Xianming.

sentences.zh: 此之三世，稱諡可也；

translations.literal: These three generations may be given posthumous titles;
translations.idiomatic: These three generations may properly receive posthumous titles;

sentences.zh: 自茲以外，未之敢聞。」

translations.literal: Beyond this, I have not dared to hear of such."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, no others deserve such honor—or so I maintain."

sentences.zh: 其三曰：「幽王死於驪山，厲王出奔於彘，未嘗隱諱，直筆書之，欲以勸善懲惡，詒誡將來。

translations.literal: The third states: "King You died at Mount Li, King Li fled to Zhi—never concealed, recorded with straight brush, wishing to encourage good and punish evil, leaving admonition for the future.
translations.idiomatic: The third principle states: "When King You died at Mount Li and King Li fled to Zhi, the historians did not conceal these events but recorded them plainly, seeking to encourage virtue and punish evil and to admonish posterity.

sentences.zh: 而太武、獻文，並遭非命，前史立紀，不異天年，言論之間，頗露首尾。

translations.literal: Yet Emperors Taiwu and Xianwen both met untimely deaths; the earlier history established their annals no differently from natural lifespan—in discourse, beginning and end were rather exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperors Taiwu and Xianwen both met violent deaths, while the earlier history recorded their reigns as though they had died natural deaths—yet in the narrative, hints of the truth show through.

sentences.zh: 殺主害君，莫知姓名，逆臣賊子，何所懼哉？

translations.literal: Who killed the lord and harmed the sovereign—no one knows the names; rebellious ministers and wicked sons—what have they to fear?
translations.idiomatic: When regicides go unnamed, what do traitorous ministers and wicked sons have to fear?

sentences.zh: 今分明直書，不敢回避。」

translations.literal: Now we record plainly with straight brush, not daring to evade."
translations.idiomatic: In the present work we record these events plainly, without evasion."

sentences.zh: 四曰：「自晉德不競，宇宙分崩，或帝或王，各自署置。

translations.literal: The fourth states: "Since Jin virtue declined, the cosmos split apart—some called themselves emperors, some kings, each establishing titles on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth principle states: "After Jin virtue declined and the realm fragmented, rulers proclaimed themselves emperors or kings as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 其生略如敵國，書死便同庶人。

translations.literal: In life they were treated roughly as rival states; in recording death they were made the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In life they were treated nearly as rival sovereigns, yet in death they were recorded no differently from commoners.

sentences.zh: 凡處華夏之地者，皆書曰卒，同之吳、楚。」

translations.literal: All who dwelt in the lands of Huaxia—all are written as 'died' (zu), equated with Wu and Chu."
translations.idiomatic: All rulers within the heartland shall be recorded with zu (died)—the same term applied to Wu and Chu."

sentences.zh: 澹又以為「司馬遷創立紀傳已來，述者非一，人無善惡，皆為立論。

translations.literal: Dan further considered: "Since Sima Qian established the annal-biography format, writers have not been few; regardless of a person's good or evil, all compose appraisals.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen further argued: "Since Sima Qian established the annal-biography format, historians have routinely composed evaluative essays on every figure, whether worthy or wicked.

sentences.zh: 計在身行跡，具在正書，事既無奇，不足懲勸，再述乍同銘頌，重敘唯覺繁文。

translations.literal: Considering that conduct and deeds are fully set out in the main text—matters being unremarkable, insufficient for admonition—re-narrating suddenly resembles inscription praise; repeating accounts only feels verbose.
translations.idiomatic: Since a person's conduct is already fully recorded in the main text, and when there is nothing remarkable to admonish by, composing another essay merely repeats what reads like an epitaph—adding only redundant prose.

sentences.zh: 案丘明亞聖之才，發揚聖旨，言'君子曰'者，無非甚泰；

translations.literal: Considering Qiu Ming's talent as second only to the Sage—expounding the Sage's intent—where he says 'the noble man says,' none fail to be greatly exalted;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Zuo Qiuming, whose talent was second only to the Sage: when he expounded the Sage's intent with 'the noble man says,' it was always to render the highest praise;

sentences.zh: 其間尋常，直言而已。

translations.literal: Among ordinary matters, he spoke directly and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary matters he simply stated the facts.

sentences.zh: 今所撰史，竊有慕焉，可為勸戒者，論其得失；

translations.literal: In the history now compiled, I privately take this as my model; where admonition is possible, I discuss gains and losses;
translations.idiomatic: In the present history I aspire to follow this model: where there is something to admonish by, I discuss gains and losses;

sentences.zh: 其無損益者，所不論也。」

translations.literal: Where there is neither gain nor loss, I do not discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Where there is nothing to admonish by, I offer no commentary."

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed it and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and expressed approval.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子罕言。

translations.literal: His son was Hanyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hanyan.

sentences.zh: 澹弟彥玄，位洧州司馬。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Yanshen served as Assistant Commander of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen, younger brother of Dan, served as military aide of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 子滿行。

translations.literal: His son was Manxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Manxing.

sentences.zh: 魏蘭根，字蘭根，收族叔也。

translations.literal: Wei Lange, courtesy name Lange, was a clansman uncle of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lange, styled Lange, was a clansman uncle of Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 父伯成，中山太守。

translations.literal: His father Bocheng was Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bocheng served as Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 蘭根身長八尺，儀貌奇偉，博學高才，機警有識悟。

translations.literal: Lange was eight chi in height, his bearing and appearance singularly imposing; widely learned with lofty talent, quick-witted and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Lange stood eight chi tall, with a singularly imposing presence. Deeply learned and highly gifted, he was quick-witted and keenly perceptive.

sentences.zh: 起家北海王國侍郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Gentleman of the Kingdom of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an attendant in the principality of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 母憂，居喪有孝稱。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he observed mourning and gained a reputation for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning and earned a reputation for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 將葬，常山郡境先有董卓祠，祠有柏樹，蘭根以卓凶逆，不應遺祠至今，乃啟刺史，請伐為槨。

translations.literal: When about to bury her, in Changshan commandery there was already a shrine to Dong Zhuo with a cypress tree; Lange considered Zhuo wicked and rebellious and that such a shrine should not remain—so he petitioned the inspector to cut it down for a coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When preparing her burial, he found a shrine to Dong Zhuo with a cypress tree still standing in Changshan commandery. Considering Zhuo a traitor whose shrine ought not to endure, he petitioned the inspector to fell the tree for his mother's coffin.

sentences.zh: 左右人言有靈，蘭根了無疑懼。

translations.literal: Those around him said the tree was numinous; Lange had not the slightest fear or hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him warned that the tree was sacred, but Lange showed not the slightest fear.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬於墓側，負土成墳，憂毀殆於滅性。

translations.literal: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to form the mound, his grief and emaciation nearly costing him his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound himself, grieving so deeply that he nearly destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 正光末，尚書令李崇為大都督，討蠕蠕，以蘭根為長史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenguang era, Minister of State Affairs Li Chong served as Grand Commander to campaign against the Rouran, appointing Lange as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, Li Chong, Minister of State Affairs, was appointed Grand Commander to campaign against the Rouran and made Lange his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 因說崇曰：「緣邊諸鎮，控攝長遠，昔時初置，地廣人稀，或徵發中原強宗子弟，或國之肺腑寄以爪牙。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Chong: "The frontier garrisons extend over vast distances. When first established, the land was broad and population sparse; some men were conscripted from powerful clans of the central plains, some were entrusted as the state's innermost loyalists and appointees as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Chong: "The frontier garrisons guard vast territories. When first established, the land was sparsely populated. Some garrison troops were drawn from powerful central plain clans; others were chosen from the empire's most trusted loyalists as its claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 中年以來，有司乖實，號曰府戶，役同廝養，官婚班齒，致失清流。

translations.literal: From mid-dynasty onward, officials diverged from fact, calling them 'household dependents,' treating their service like that of servants and stable hands, arranging marriages by official rank and seniority, causing them to lose their standing among the pure current.
translations.idiomatic: From the mid-dynasty onward, officials misrepresented their status, designating them as garrison households and treating their service like that of servants. Marriage was arranged by bureaucratic rank rather than pedigree, stripping them of their standing among the elite.

sentences.zh: 而本宗舊類，各各榮顯，顧瞻彼此，理當憤怨。

translations.literal: Yet their original clans and old associates each achieved glory and prominence; looking at one another, indignation and resentment were only natural.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile their clansmen back in the central plains rose to eminence one after another. Comparisons between the two groups naturally bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 宜改鎮立州，分置郡縣。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to convert garrisons into prefectures and establish commanderies and counties separately.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons should be converted into prefectures and subdivided into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 凡是府戶，悉免為平人，入仕次第，一準其舊。

translations.literal: All garrison household dependents should be released to become ordinary people; their entry into office should follow the same order as before.
translations.idiomatic: All garrison households should be granted ordinary civilian status, with official advancement restored to its original criteria.

sentences.zh: 此計若行，國家庶無北顧之慮。」

translations.literal: If this plan were implemented, the state would presumably have no concern of looking northward in anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: If this plan were adopted, the state would no longer need to worry about its northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 崇以奏聞，事寢不報。

translations.literal: Chong memorialized this to the throne; the matter was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted the proposal to the throne, but it was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，為岐州刺史，從行台蕭實夤討破宛川。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, he served as Inspector of Qizhou, following the Mobile Headquarters of Xiao Baoyin to defeat and pacify Wanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era he was appointed Inspector of Qizhou and accompanied Xiao Baoyin's field headquarters in the suppression of Wanchuan.

sentences.zh: 俘其人為奴婢，以美女十人賞蘭根。

translations.literal: Captives were made slaves and servants; ten beautiful women were rewarded to Lange.
translations.idiomatic: The captives were taken as slaves, and ten beautiful women were offered to Lange as a reward.

sentences.zh: 蘭根辭曰：「此縣介於強虜，故成背叛。

translations.literal: Lange declined, saying: "This county lay between powerful enemies, thus it came to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Lange declined, saying: "This county rebelled because it was caught between powerful enemies.

sentences.zh: 今當恤其饑寒，奈何並充僕隸？」

translations.literal: Now we should show compassion for their hunger and cold—how can we make them all servants and slaves?"
translations.idiomatic: They should now be relieved from hunger and cold. How can we turn them all into slaves?"

sentences.zh: 於是盡以歸其父兄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned them all to their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned them all to their families.

sentences.zh: 部內麥多五穗。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction wheat often bore five ears per stalk.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction wheat often bore five ears to the stalk—a sign of abundance.

sentences.zh: 鄰州田鼠為災，犬牙不入岐境。

translations.literal: Field mice plagued neighboring prefectures, but their incursions did not cross into Qizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Field mice ravaged neighboring prefectures, but did not enter Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤敗於涇州，岐州人囚蘭根降賊。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jingzhou, the people of Qizhou imprisoned Lange and surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jingzhou, the people of Qizhou imprisoned Lange and submitted to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 寶夤兵威復振，城人復斬賊刺史侯莫陳仲和，推蘭根復任。

translations.literal: Baoyin's military prestige revived; the city people again beheaded the rebel Inspector Houmo Chen Zhonghe and restored Lange to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin's forces rallied, the city people killed the rebel inspector Houmo Chen Zhonghe and reinstated Lange.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以蘭根得西土人心，加都督涇、岐、東秦、南岐四州諸軍事，兼四州行台尚書。

translations.literal: The court, because Lange had won the hearts of the western territories, added him as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for Jing, Qi, Eastern Qin, and Southern Qi prefectures, concurrently Mobile Headquarters Minister for the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court, recognizing that Lange commanded the loyalty of the western territories, appointed him Commander-in-Chief over the four prefectures of Jing, Qi, Eastern Qin, and Southern Qi, and concurrently Mobile Headquarters Minister for all four.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，河北流人南度，以蘭根兼尚書，使齊、濟、二兗四州安撫，並置郡縣。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, refugees from Hebei fled south; Lange was appointed concurrent Minister and sent to pacify Qi, Ji, and the two Yanzhou regions, simultaneously establishing commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, refugees from Hebei flooded southward. Lange was appointed concurrent Minister and charged with pacifying Qi, Ji, and the two Yan prefectures, establishing commanderies and counties as needed.

sentences.zh: 蘭根甥邢杲反於青、光間，復詔蘭根慰勞。

translations.literal: Lange's nephew Xing Shao rebelled between Qing and Guang; again Lange was ordered by imperial edict to offer consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When Lange's nephew Xing Shao rebelled in Qing and Guang provinces, Lange was again ordered to go and negotiate with him.

sentences.zh: 杲不下，仍隨元天穆討之。

translations.literal: Shao would not submit; Lange then followed Yuan Tianmu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao refused to surrender, and Lange joined Yuan Tianmu's campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜中書令。

translations.literal: On return, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊帝之將誅爾硃榮，蘭根泄之于兄子周達，周達告爾硃世隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was about to execute Erzhu Rong, Lange leaked it to his nephew Zhou Da; Zhou Da informed Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was plotting to kill Erzhu Rong, Lange leaked the plan to his nephew Zhou Da, who informed Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，蘭根憂，不知所出。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Lange was anxious and knew not what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, Lange was deeply anxious and uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 時應詔王道習見信于莊帝，蘭根乃托附之，求出立功。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Daoxi, who answered imperial summons, enjoyed Emperor Zhuang's trust; Lange therefore attached himself to Wang, seeking to go out and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daoxi, a court confidant of Emperor Zhuang, was then in favor. Lange attached himself to Wang and sought a field assignment where he might redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 乃兼尚書右僕射、河北行台，定州率募鄉曲，欲防井陘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Mobile Headquarters of Hebei; at Dingzhou he raised local militia, intending to guard Jingxing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Hebei Mobile Headquarters Minister, and at Dingzhou he raised local militia to defend Jingxing Pass.

sentences.zh: 為榮將侯深所敗，走依勃海高乾。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Rong's general Hou Shen and fled to take refuge with Gao Gan of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated by Rong's general Hou Shen and fled to Gao Gan of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 屬乾兄弟義舉，固在其中。

translations.literal: When the Gao brothers raised their righteous enterprise, he was naturally among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gao brothers launched their uprising, he naturally joined them.

sentences.zh: 神武以宿望深禮之。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because of his longstanding reputation, treated him with deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, respecting his long-standing reputation, treated him with deep honor.

sentences.zh: 中興初，為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing, he served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhongxing era he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 神武將入洛陽，時廢立未決，令蘭根察節閔帝。

translations.literal: When Shenwu was about to enter Luoyang, the decision to depose or install was not yet settled; he ordered Lange to observe Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: As Gao Huan prepared to enter Luoyang with the question of deposition still unresolved, he dispatched Lange to assess Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 帝神采高明，蘭根恐於後難測，遂與高乾兄弟及黃門侍郎崔甗同請。

translations.literal: The emperor's bearing and spirit were clear and lofty; Lange feared he would be hard to gauge later, and therefore joined with the Gao brothers and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Yan in petitioning together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's bearing was sharp and commanding. Fearing he would prove unpredictable, Lange joined the Gao brothers and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Yan in recommending his removal.

sentences.zh: 神武不得已，遂立武帝。

translations.literal: Shenwu had no choice and therefore installed Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, left with no alternative, installed Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，加侍中、開府儀同三司、钜鹿縣侯，啟授兄子周達。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was added Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Aide of the Three Palaces, Marquis of Julu County; he petitioned to grant his nephew Zhou Da an office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal, and Marquis of Julu, and petitioned to confer office on his nephew Zhou Da.

sentences.zh: 蘭根既預勳業，位居端副，始敘復岐州勳，封永興侯。

translations.literal: Lange having participated in the meritorious enterprise and holding the foremost vice position, for the first time his Qizhou merit was recorded and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Having shared in the founding enterprise and holding a senior vice-ministerial post, Lange at last had his Qizhou service recognized and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 高乾之死，蘭根懼，以病免。

translations.literal: At Gao Gan's death, Lange was fearful and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Gan's execution, Lange, fearing for himself, resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 天平初，言病篤，以開府儀同歸本鄉，門施行馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, claiming grave illness, he returned to his native place with Grand Master ceremonial status; horses were posted at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era, citing grave illness, he returned home with full ceremonial honors; horses were stationed at his gate as a mark of rank.

sentences.zh: 武定三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuding, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Duke of the Ministry of Education; posthumous title Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title Duke of Education with the posthumous name Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 長子相如襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xiangru inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xiangru inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 相如性亢直，有文藻，與族兄愷齊名，雅為當時所貴。

translations.literal: Xiangru's character was forthright and unyielding; he had literary talent and was equally famed with his clansman elder brother Kai, both esteemed by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru was upright and outspoken, possessed of literary gifts, and shared equal renown with his clansman Kai—both were held in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 孝昭時，佐命功臣配饗，不及蘭根，次子敬仲表訴，竟不允。

translations.literal: During the Xiaozhao era, founding ministers were granted ancestral sacrifice; Lange was not included; his second son Jingzhong submitted a petition of complaint, but it was ultimately not granted.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaozhao's reign, founding ministers were granted ancestral rites, but Lange was excluded. His second son Jingzhong petitioned on his behalf, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 敬仲以才器稱，卒于章武太守。

translations.literal: Jingzhong was known for talent and capacity; he died as Administrator of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong was noted for talent and ability and died while serving as Administrator of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 子餉，字孝衡。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang, courtesy name Xiaoheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang, styled Xiaoheng.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，學涉有時譽，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his learning was broad and he enjoyed contemporary repute; he was known for filial piety in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at a young age, he was broadly learned and enjoyed a contemporary reputation; he was known for filial devotion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 隋饒州司倉參軍事。

translations.literal: Under Sui he served as Military Assistant for Granaries of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as granary officer of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 子景義、景禮並有才行，鄉人呼為雙鳳，早卒。

translations.literal: His sons Jingyi and Jingli both had talent and conduct; townspeople called them the Twin Phoenixes; they died young.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jingyi and Jingli both possessed talent and character; their townspeople called them the Twin Phoenixes. They died young.

sentences.zh: 敬仲弟少政，位至洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's younger brother Shaozheng reached the post of Inspector of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's younger brother Shaozheng rose to Inspector of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 子孝該、孝幾。

translations.literal: His sons were Xiaogai and Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiaogai and Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 愷自散騎常侍遷青州長史，固辭。

translations.literal: Kai was transferred from Attendant Cavalry Regular to Chief Administrator of Qingzhou and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was transferred from Attendant Cavalry Regular to Chief Administrator of Qingzhou, but firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 文宣大怒曰：「何物漢子，與官不就！」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan raged: "What sort of Han fellow refuses an office when offered!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan flew into a rage: "What kind of Han wretch refuses an appointment when one is offered!"

sentences.zh: 時帝已失德，朝廷為之懼，愷容色坦然。

translations.literal: By then the emperor had lost virtue; the court feared for Kai, but his bearing remained untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already fallen into debauchery, and the court trembled for Kai's safety, but he remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「死與長史，任卿所擇。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Death or chief administrator—choose as you will."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Death or the chief administrator's post—choose as you please."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「能殺臣者陛下，不受長史者愚臣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Only Your Majesty can kill your subject; only a foolish subject would refuse the chief administrator's post."
translations.idiomatic: Kai replied: "Only Your Majesty may take my life; only a fool would accept the chief administrator's post."

sentences.zh: 帝謂楊愔曰：「何慮無人，苦用此漢！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yang Yin: "Why worry about lacking men—why insist on using this Han fellow!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yang Yin: "Are we so short of men that we must bother with this Han wretch!

sentences.zh: 放還，永不須收。」

translations.literal: Release him and never employ him again."
translations.idiomatic: Release him—and never summon him again."

sentences.zh: 由是積年沈廢。

translations.literal: Thereafter for many years he languished in disuse.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he languished in obscurity for many years.

sentences.zh: 後遇愔于路，微自陳。

translations.literal: Later he encountered Yin on the road and briefly pleaded his case.
translations.idiomatic: Later he encountered Yang Yin on the road and briefly made his case.

sentences.zh: 愔云：「咸由中旨。」

translations.literal: Yin said: "All was by imperial decree."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "That was entirely by imperial decree."

sentences.zh: 愷應聲曰；

translations.literal: Kai responded immediately, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Kai answered at once:

sentences.zh: 「雖復零雨自天，終待雲興四嶽，公豈得言不知？」

translations.literal: "Though scattered rain may fall from heaven, in the end one must wait for clouds to rise from the four peaks—can you, sir, say you do not know?"
translations.idiomatic: "Even when rain falls from heaven, clouds must still gather on the four peaks—surely you cannot claim ignorance?"

sentences.zh: 楊愔欣然曰：「此言極為簡要。」

translations.literal: Yang Yin said with pleasure: "These words are most concise and apt."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin smiled and said: "Well put—and admirably concise."

sentences.zh: 數日，除霍州刺史，在職有政理。

translations.literal: Within days he was appointed Inspector of Huozhou; in office he had good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was appointed Inspector of Huozhou, where he governed effectively.

sentences.zh: 後卒于膠州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：伯起少頗疏放，不拘行檢，及折節讀書，鬱為偉器。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Boqi in youth was rather free and unrestrained, not bound by conduct; when he bent himself to reading, he became a grand vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In youth Boqi was rather dissolute and unconstrained in conduct, but when he applied himself to study he ripened into a man of great capacity.

sentences.zh: 學博今古，才極從橫，體物之旨，尤為富贍，足以入相如之室，游尼父之門。

translations.literal: His learning spanned past and present; his talent reached the utmost in versatility; his intent in embodying things was especially rich and ample—sufficient to enter Sima Xiangru's chamber and roam in Confucius's gate.
translations.idiomatic: His learning spanned antiquity and the present; his talent was prodigiously versatile, and his descriptive power especially rich—worthy of a place beside Sima Xiangru and at the threshold of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 勒成魏籍，追從班、馬，婉而有則，繁而不蕪，持論序言，鉤深致遠。

translations.literal: Compiling the Wei record, following Ban and Sima—graceful yet with principle, elaborate yet not redundant; holding to argument in prefaces and appraisals, probing deep and reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: In compiling the history of Wei he followed in the footsteps of Ban Gu and Sima Qian—elegant yet principled, elaborate yet never excessive; his prefaces and appraisals probed deep and reached far.

sentences.zh: 但意存實錄，好抵陰私，到於親故之家，一無所說，不平之議，見於斯矣。

translations.literal: Yet his intent was to preserve truthful records; he loved to expose hidden private failings—to the point that among close kin and old friends he had nothing good to say; charges of unfairness appear here.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his commitment to truthful recording led him to expose private failings, even among kin and old friends—and the complaints of bias are evident here.

sentences.zh: 王松年、李庶等並論正家門，未為謗議，遂憑附時宰，鼓動淫刑，庶因鞭撻而終，此公之失德。

translations.literal: Wang Songnian, Li Shu, and others all discussed correcting family conduct—not yet slander—yet by relying on the reigning minister he incited excessive punishments; Shu died from flogging—this was the gentleman's failure in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Songnian, Li Shu, and others had merely argued for moral reform in their own households, not slander—yet by allying with the chief minister he incited savage punishments; Li Shu died under the lash. This was his moral failing.

sentences.zh: 長賢思樹風聲，抗言昏俗，有硃子遊之風。

translations.literal: Changxian thought to establish a reputation for upright influence, speaking out against corrupt custom—he had the air of Master Zhu's wanderings.
translations.idiomatic: Changxian sought to uphold upright standards and spoke boldly against a debased age, evoking the spirit of Zhu Yun.

sentences.zh: 季景父子，雅業相傳，抑弓冶之義。

translations.literal: Jijing and his son—elegant craft passed down, affirming the meaning of bow-making and smelting.
translations.idiomatic: Jijing and his son carried on a refined literary tradition in the spirit of the craftsman passing his art to his son.

sentences.zh: 蘭根道冠時英，功參霸業，亦一代之偉人也。

translations.literal: Lange's conduct crowned the heroes of the age; his merit shared in the hegemonic enterprise—truly a great man of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Lange's character stood above the eminent men of his age; his achievements contributed to the founding of a new dynasty—truly a great man of his generation.
